the unusual tomato plant, which they were secretly competing to claim.
the committee's rules, which they hoped to have rewritten that summer.
input.design: Two facts must be connected: the obsessive fence quarrel and the total neglect of a fruitful plant directly overhead. Distractors B and D echo real details from the argument, and C overreads the tomato's presence.
input.explanation: 이웃들은 몇 시간씩 울타리 문제로 다투면서도 머리 위에 열매가 주렁주렁 달린 토마토는 한 번도 올려다보지 않는다. 이 두 사실을 함께 보면, 그들이 진짜 신경 쓰는 것은 정원의 수확이 아니라 다툼 그 자체라는 결론이 나오므로 A가 정답이다. B는 지문에 나온 콩의 그늘 문제를 가져왔지만, 콩을 정말 걱정하는 사람이 눈앞의 열매를 무시한다는 점과 맞지 않는다. C는 두 사람이 토마토를 전혀 보지 않았다는 서술과 모순된다. D는 규정을 읽는 행동에 근거하지만, 규정을 바꾸려 한다는 내용은 지문에 없고 그레타가 관찰한 대비도 설명하지 못한다.
input.explanation_en: The neighbors argue about the fence for hours, yet neither one looks up at the tomato plant full of ripe fruit hanging right above them. When you put those two facts together, it's clear they care about the argument itself, not about anything the garden grows, so A is correct. B uses the detail about shade on the beans, but someone who truly cared about crops wouldn't ignore ripe fruit right over their head. C contradicts the text, which says neither neighbor ever looked up at the tomato. D builds on the neighbors reading the bylaws aloud, but the text never says they want the rules changed, and that idea doesn't explain the contrast Greta notices.

input.passage: Sociologist Erving Goffman argued that everyday interaction resembles a theatrical performance: people manage the impressions others form of them, maintaining a "front stage" demeanor before audiences and relaxing in "backstage" regions. Many readers have taken this to mean that Goffman saw social life as fundamentally deceptive, with individuals cynically manipulating one another. __Yet Goffman stressed that most performers are taken in by their own acts, sincerely believing in the roles they play, and that sustaining "face" is a cooperative effort in which audiences tactfully overlook slips to spare everyone embarrassment.__ On this reading, his dramaturgy describes less a world of con artists than a shared moral order, one that participants jointly uphold even in rigid institutional settings such as hospitals and schools.
input.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It presents aspects of Goffman's account that undercut a common interpretation of his work and prepare the text's alternative reading.
It presents an example of cynical manipulation that supports a common interpretation of Goffman's view of social life.
It presents a criticism of Goffman's theatrical model that the text goes on to show applies mainly to institutional settings.
It presents the distinction between front stage and backstage regions that the text treats as the core of Goffman's theory.
input.explanation: 밑줄 문장은 'Yet'으로 시작해 고프먼이 사회생활을 기만으로 보았다는 흔한 해석을 반박하는 근거(진실한 역할 수행, 협력적 체면 유지)를 제시하고, 이어지는 '공유된 도덕 질서'라는 대안적 해석으로 연결되므로 A가 정답이다. B는 냉소적 조작이라는 소재는 맞지만 밑줄 문장은 그 해석을 지지하지 않고 약화시킨다. C는 기관 환경이 지문에 나오지만 밑줄 문장은 고프먼 모델에 대한 비판이 아니라 그의 주장 자체이다. D는 전무대/후무대 구분이 첫 문장에서 소개된 내용이지 밑줄 문장의 기능이 아니다.
input.explanation_en: The underlined sentence opens with "Yet" and points to parts of Goffman's account (performers sincerely believing in their roles, face being kept up cooperatively) that challenge the common view that he saw social life as deceptive. It also sets up the next sentence's alternative reading of a "shared moral order," so A is correct. B mentions cynical manipulation, but the sentence weakens that interpretation instead of supporting it. C picks up on institutional settings, but the sentence isn't a criticism of Goffman's model; it states his own position. D refers to the front stage/backstage distinction, which comes from the first sentence and isn't what the underlined sentence does.
input.design: To answer, students have to connect the sentence's contrast with the earlier interpretation to the alternative reading that follows it. The wrong answers borrow real details from the passage (manipulation, institutions, front stage) but misstate what the sentence does.

input.passage: Art historians have long linked Caravaggio's tenebrism—his practice of setting brightly lit figures against near-total darkness—to the goals of the Counter-Reformation Church, which urged painters to make sacred stories emotionally gripping for ordinary worshippers. In The Calling of Saint Matthew (1599–1600), a single shaft of light cuts across a dim tax office and falls on Matthew at the instant Christ summons him. __Yet technical studies of Caravaggio's canvases suggest that this effect began less as a theological program than as a studio habit: he often posed models in a darkened room lit by one high window or lamp.__ Some scholars therefore argue that the painting's spiritual intensity grew out of a practical working method that patrons later found well suited to devotional aims, rather than from a deliberate plan to illustrate Church doctrine.
input.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It offers an example of how the Counter-Reformation Church instructed painters to arrange the lighting in their studios.
It describes a feature of The Calling of Saint Matthew that supports the long-standing view that Caravaggio designed tenebrism to serve doctrine.
It identifies the specific religious moment that Caravaggio chose to emphasize with light in The Calling of Saint Matthew.
It introduces evidence that complicates a widely held explanation of where Caravaggio's lighting technique came from.
input.explanation: 밑줄 문장은 'Yet'으로 시작하며, 테네브리즘이 반종교개혁의 목표에서 나왔다는 오랜 견해와 달리 작업실 습관에서 비롯되었다는 기술적 연구 결과를 제시하므로 D가 정답이다. A는 교회와 작업실 조명이라는 두 요소를 섞었지만, 교회가 작업실 조명을 지시했다는 내용은 지문에 없다. B는 그림의 특징을 언급한다는 점은 맞지만, 이 문장은 기존 견해를 뒷받침하는 것이 아니라 그 견해에 의문을 제기한다. C에서 말하는 소명의 순간은 밑줄 문장이 아니라 그 앞 문장에서 묘사된다.
input.explanation_en: The underlined sentence starts with "Yet" and brings in technical findings that the effect came from a studio habit. That challenges the long-held view that tenebrism grew out of Counter-Reformation goals, so D is correct. A mixes up two things in the text, the Church and studio lighting, but the passage never says the Church told painters how to light their studios. B is right that the sentence relates to the painting, but the sentence questions the traditional view instead of supporting it. C describes the moment of the calling, which appears in the sentence before the underlined one, not in the underlined sentence itself.
input.design: To answer, the reader has to connect the contrast signal "Yet" with how the claim about origins changes. Choices A and B reuse real details from the passage so that a quick skim makes them look right. Choice C points to the sentence next to the underlined one.

input.passage: Graphene aerogels are among the lightest solids ever produced: some samples have densities below 0.2 milligrams per cubic centimeter, lighter than the air they contain. To make them, researchers typically freeze a suspension of graphene oxide sheets and then remove the ice by sublimation, leaving behind a porous three-dimensional network of carbon walls. Many observers assumed that a material this airy would be too fragile for practical use. __Yet compression tests revealed that some of these aerogels can be squeezed to less than a fifth of their original height and then spring back almost completely, cycle after cycle.__ Materials scientists attribute this resilience to the way the graphene sheets bend at their junctions instead of fracturing, a finding that has prompted interest in using the aerogels as shock absorbers and as reusable sponges for oil spills.
input.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It describes a step in the manufacturing process that explains why graphene aerogels have such low densities.
It presents an observation that the researchers later attribute to a flaw in their testing methods.
It provides a measurement that establishes graphene aerogels as lighter than any other known solid.
It offers evidence that challenges an expectation and sets up the explanation that follows.
input.explanation: 밑줄 문장은 'Yet'으로 시작해, 이렇게 가벼운 물질은 너무 약할 것이라는 앞 문장의 예상을 압축 실험 결과로 반박하며, 다음 문장은 그 복원력의 원인(접합부에서 휘어짐)을 설명한다. 따라서 D가 정답이다. A는 제조 과정(동결·승화)이 앞에서 설명되긴 하지만 밑줄 문장은 제조 단계가 아니라 실험 결과이다. B는 관찰을 다루는 점은 맞으나, 지문은 그 결과를 실험 결함이 아닌 그래핀 시트의 휘어짐으로 설명한다. C는 밀도 수치를 다루는데, 그것은 밑줄 문장이 아니라 첫 문장의 내용이다.
input.explanation_en: The underlined sentence begins with "Yet," signaling that it contradicts the previous sentence's assumption that such an airy material would be too fragile, and the following sentence then explains the cause of this resilience (sheets bending at junctions). So D is correct. A is wrong because, although the freeze-and-sublimate process is described earlier, the underlined sentence reports a test result, not a manufacturing step. B correctly notes that the sentence reports an observation, but the text attributes the result to the bending of graphene sheets, not to a testing flaw. C is wrong because the density measurement appears in the first sentence, not the underlined one.
input.design: 오답 A·C는 지문의 다른 문장 내용(제조·밀도)을 끌어와 부분 근거를 갖게 했고, B는 '관찰'이라는 맞는 요소에 틀린 후속 해석을 결합했다. 정답은 앞 문장의 예상과 뒤 문장의 설명을 모두 연결해야 확정된다.

input.passage: During hibernation, Arctic ground squirrels allow their core body temperature to fall below 0°C, lower than that recorded in any other mammal. Yet roughly every two to three weeks, each animal briefly rewarms to near 37°C before sinking back into torpor. Researchers long assumed that shivering muscles supplied most of the heat for these arousals. __Measurements of tissue temperature during rewarming, however, showed that deposits of brown adipose tissue between the shoulder blades heated up well before the skeletal muscles did.__ Biologist Kelly Drew and colleagues have since proposed that this specialized fat, which converts stored energy directly into heat, starts each arousal, with shivering joining in only after the brain and heart have been partly rewarmed.
input.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It presents a finding that explains why Arctic ground squirrels can survive body temperatures below 0°C.
It presents a finding that confirms researchers' earlier view about how arousals from torpor are powered.
It presents a finding that shows how often Arctic ground squirrels rewarm during hibernation.
It presents a finding that challenges an earlier assumption and sets up the explanation that follows.
input.explanation: 밑줄 문장은 'however'로 시작하며, 떨림 근육이 열을 공급한다는 기존 가정과 달리 갈색지방이 먼저 데워진다는 측정 결과를 제시하고, 이어지는 Drew의 제안의 근거가 되므로 D가 정답이다. A는 0°C 이하 생존이 지문에 나오지만 밑줄 문장은 그 이유가 아니라 재가온 과정을 다룬다. B는 측정이 기존 견해를 확인한 것이 아니라 반박했으므로 틀리다. C의 재가온 빈도는 앞 문장에서 제시된 정보이다.
input.explanation_en: The underlined sentence begins with "however" and reports that brown fat warmed before muscle, contradicting the assumption that shivering powered arousals; it then grounds Drew's proposal, so D is correct. A is wrong because the sub-zero survival is mentioned, but the sentence addresses rewarming, not how the squirrels endure cold. B reverses the relationship: the finding undercuts, rather than confirms, the earlier view. C describes information given in an earlier sentence, not the underlined one.
input.design: 오답 A·C는 지문 속 실제 정보를 끌어와 부분적 근거를 갖고, B는 '기존 견해'와 연결되지만 방향이 반대라 'however'와 이후 문장 연결을 확인해야 배제된다.

input.passage: In the 1970s, anthropologist Barbara Myerhoff spent several years at a senior center in Venice, California, whose members were mostly elderly Jewish immigrants from Eastern Europe. Many observers had described such communities as remnants, groups simply waiting out the end of a vanishing way of life. Myerhoff noticed something else: the members kept inventing ceremonies, such as a graduation for a class of elderly students and a birthday celebration for a ninety-five-year-old man, that mixed religious forms with entirely secular content. __Few of these events followed any traditional script, and some participants openly admitted that they no longer believed in the religious teachings the ceremonies borrowed from.__ For Myerhoff, this was exactly what made the rituals revealing. Because the members could not count on inherited meaning, they had to build meaning themselves, and their improvised ceremonies showed a community actively deciding who it was rather than passively fading away.
input.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It gives evidence supporting the observers' view that the community was a remnant of a disappearing way of life.
It explains why Myerhoff eventually concluded that the ceremonies held little real significance for their participants.
It points out features of the ceremonies that might seem to weaken their importance but that Myerhoff treated as central to her interpretation.
It describes a disagreement among the center's members about whether the ceremonies should follow religious tradition.
input.explanation: 밑줄 문장은 의식이 전통 형식을 따르지 않고 참여자들이 종교적 가르침을 믿지 않았다는 점을 제시하는데, 언뜻 보면 의식의 가치를 깎는 듯한 특징이다. 하지만 바로 다음 문장에서 Myerhoff는 바로 이 점이 의식을 의미 있게 만든다고 보았으므로 C가 정답이다. A는 '사라져 가는 공동체'라는 관찰자들의 견해와 연결되지만, 이 글은 그 견해를 반박한다. B는 밑줄 문장만 보면 그럴듯하지만, Myerhoff의 결론은 정반대이다. D는 구성원 사이의 의견 차이를 언급하지만, 지문에는 그런 논쟁이 나오지 않는다.
input.explanation_en: The underlined sentence says the ceremonies didn't follow tradition and that some participants didn't believe the teachings behind them. At first glance, those details seem to make the rituals less important. But the very next sentence tells you that Myerhoff saw exactly this as what made them revealing, so C is correct. A ties in with the observers' "remnant" view, but the text pushes back against that view instead of supporting it. B might sound reasonable if you read the sentence on its own, but Myerhoff actually concluded the opposite. D mentions a disagreement among the members, and the text never describes one.
input.design: To get this right, you have to read the underlined sentence together with the sentence after it, which reverses how it first seems. A and B draw on details that look like they support them.

input.passage: In the 1920s and 1930s, Swiss psychologist Jean Piaget questioned children individually rather than giving them standardized tests. In a typical conservation task, a child watched as water was poured from a short, wide glass into a tall, thin one and was then asked whether the amount had changed. Many five-year-olds insisted that the tall glass held more. __Piaget, however, was less interested in whether a child answered correctly than in the reasoning the child offered when he pressed with follow-up questions such as "How do you know?"__ Those explanations showed him that younger children tended to focus on a single visible dimension, such as height, while older children reasoned that nothing had been added or taken away. From such patterns, Piaget argued that children's thinking moves through distinct stages.
input.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It presents a common error made by young children that the rest of the text treats as evidence against Piaget's stage theory.
It identifies the aspect of the children's responses that made possible the observations described in the following sentence.
It explains why Piaget chose to replace the conservation task with standardized tests in his later research.
It provides the result of the water-pouring task that leads directly to Piaget's conclusion in the final sentence.
input.explanation: 밑줄 문장은 피아제가 정답 여부보다 아이들이 내놓는 추론(설명)에 주목했다는 점을 밝히고, 바로 다음 문장은 그 설명들을 통해 연령별 사고 차이를 발견했다고 이어지므로 B가 정답이다. A는 아이들의 오류가 앞 문장에 나오긴 하지만 밑줄 문장은 오류 자체를 제시하지 않으며, 지문은 그것을 이론에 반하는 증거로 다루지도 않는다. C는 지문 첫 문장에서 피아제가 표준화 검사를 쓰지 않았다고 했으므로 반대 방향이다. D는 밑줄 문장이 과제의 결과가 아니라 연구자의 관심 초점을 말하며, 결론과 바로 연결되는 것은 그 다음 문장의 관찰이므로 틀렸다.
input.explanation_en: The underlined sentence says Piaget cared more about children's reasoning than about whether their answers were correct, and the very next sentence explains what those explanations showed him, so B is correct. A is wrong because the children's error actually appears in the sentence before, not in the underlined one, and the text never treats it as evidence against Piaget's theory. C contradicts the text, which says Piaget avoided standardized tests. D is wrong because the underlined sentence describes Piaget's focus, not the task's result; the observations that lead to his conclusion come in the sentence after it.
input.design: Two-step judgment: recognize the sentence shifts focus from answers to reasoning, then link it to the next sentence's findings. A and D draw on nearby true content (the error, the conclusion) to tempt skimmers.

input.passage: Tardigrades, microscopic animals often called water bears, can survive almost complete drying by entering a state known as anhydrobiosis. As water leaves their bodies, they pull in their legs and contract into a compact form called a tun, and their metabolism slows to levels that can barely be detected. For years, researchers assumed that tardigrades, like brine shrimp and some nematodes, protected their cells mainly by filling them with the sugar trehalose, which turns into a glassy solid that holds delicate structures in place. However, many tardigrade species produce little or no trehalose. In 2017, biologist Thomas Boothby and colleagues reported that tardigrades instead rely on a family of proteins found only in their group, called tardigrade-specific intrinsically disordered proteins (TDPs). When genes for these proteins were silenced, the animals no longer survived drying well, and when the proteins were added to yeast and bacteria, those organisms became more tolerant of desiccation. Like trehalose, the proteins appear to form a glass-like matrix as cells dry, which suggests that tardigrades arrived at a familiar protective strategy by using a very different molecule.
input.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Tardigrades survive drying mainly by contracting into a tun and slowing their metabolism, which makes the chemical makeup of their cells less important than researchers once believed.
Tardigrades protect their cells during drying by producing larger amounts of trehalose than brine shrimp and nematodes do, which explains why they tolerate harsher conditions.
Tardigrades appear to protect their cells during drying with proteins unique to their group, which seem to work much as trehalose does in other animals.
Tardigrade proteins have been shown to make yeast and bacteria more tolerant of drying, which suggests the proteins may soon be widely used to preserve other organisms.
input.explanation: 이 지문은 트레할로스가 주된 보호 수단이라는 기존 가정을 소개한 뒤, 타디그레이드는 고유 단백질(TDP)에 의존하며 이 단백질이 트레할로스처럼 유리 같은 기질을 만든다는 점을 제시하므로 C가 정답이다. A는 툰 형성과 대사 저하라는 지문의 세부 내용을 다루지만, 화학적 보호가 덜 중요하다는 주장은 지문에 없다. B는 트레할로스를 언급하지만, 지문은 많은 종이 트레할로스를 거의 만들지 않는다고 말하므로 지문과 모순된다. D는 효모·세균 실험이라는 근거 하나만 보고 지문에 없는 미래 응용까지 추론한 것이다.
input.explanation_en: C is correct. The passage first describes the old assumption that trehalose was the main protection, then reports that tardigrades rely on their own unique proteins (TDPs), which seem to form a glassy matrix the same way trehalose does. A uses real details from the passage, the tun and the slowed metabolism, but the passage never says that cell chemistry matters less. B mentions trehalose, but it contradicts the passage, which says many species make little or no trehalose. D takes one supporting detail, the yeast and bacteria experiment, and adds a prediction about future uses that the passage never makes.
input.design: To answer, students have to connect two ideas: the old trehalose assumption being replaced, and the new proteins working in a similar way. The wrong choices either use true details while missing the main point (A, D) or misread the trehalose detail (B), and all four choices share the same "Tardigrades... which..." sentence structure.

input.passage: Captain Elias Merrow had spent three nights at the chart table drawing the river from Cairo to Natchez, marking every sandbar and snag he had learned in twenty years of piloting. When his brother Tobias finally came up to the pilothouse, Elias pushed the folded sheet across the wheel without a word. Tobias, who had not spoken to him since their father's funeral and who had boarded the boat only because no other passage south was ______ the map open slowly, as if it might tear.
input.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: available; unfolded
available, and unfolded
available unfolded
available, unfolded
input.design: 문장 주어 Tobias와 동사 unfolded 사이에 'who...who...' 비필수 관계절 두 개를 길게 끼워 넣어, 수식어를 닫는 쉼표가 필요함을 판단하게 했다. 세미콜론과 'and' 오답은 각각 절 경계 규칙처럼 보여 부분적으로 그럴듯하다.
input.explanation: 이 문장의 주어는 Tobias이고 본동사는 unfolded이며, 그 사이의 'who had not spoken... available'은 앞쪽 쉼표로 열린 비필수 관계절이다. 따라서 이 삽입절을 닫는 쉼표 하나가 필요하므로 D가 정답이다. A의 세미콜론은 앞뒤에 독립절이 있어야 하는데, 앞부분은 주어만 있고 동사가 없는 불완전한 절이다. B의 'and'는 unfolded를 관계절 속 동사(had boarded)와 나란히 묶어 버려 주어 Tobias에게 본동사가 남지 않는다. C는 삽입절을 닫는 쉼표가 빠져 있어 'available unfolded'가 잘못 붙어 읽힌다.
input.explanation_en: The subject of this sentence is Tobias and its main verb is unfolded. Between them sits a nonessential relative clause ("who had not spoken... available") that opens with a comma, so it needs a matching comma to close it, which makes D correct. A uses a semicolon, but a semicolon needs an independent clause on each side, and the part before it has a subject with no main verb. B adds "and," which pairs unfolded with the verb inside the relative clause (had boarded), so Tobias ends up with no main verb. C leaves out the closing comma, so the clause never ends and "available unfolded" runs together.

input.passage:
The following is adapted from a scene in a 1950s novel set in Paris.

On the last Thursday of October 1952, Monsieur Aubert, who had come into Lucien Ferrand's bookshop every week for eleven years, set a parcel on the counter and left without his usual remark about the weather. Inside was a copy of Montaigne's Essays, its spine cracked, its corners soft as felt, a coffee ring blooming across the title page. Lucien turned it over twice. To give a bookseller a ruined book, he thought, was to tell him that his trade was worth nothing more than this. He slid the volume beneath the counter and did not look at it again that day.

Discussing this scene, literary scholar Hélène Marchetti argues that the novel invites readers to see what Lucien cannot: that the book's battered condition is itself the message, evidence of a devotion that Aubert built over many years and connected directly to Lucien.
input.question: Which finding, if true, would most directly support Marchetti's argument?
options: In a later chapter, Lucien realizes he misjudged Aubert and visits his apartment to say sorry, but finds that Aubert has moved away from Paris.
In a later chapter, Lucien remembers that his own father, also a bookseller, believed that no customer should ever give a used book as a gift.
In a later chapter, Lucien learns that Aubert first bought the volume at a different shop across the Seine before he started visiting Lucien's store.
In a later chapter, Lucien opens the volume and finds Aubert's dated notes in its margins, many responding to passages Lucien had recommended to him over the years.
input.explanation: Marchetti의 주장에는 두 부분이 있다. 책이 낡은 것은 Aubert가 오랜 세월 쌓아 온 헌신의 증거라는 점, 그리고 그 헌신이 Lucien과 직접 이어져 있다는 점이다. D는 여러 해에 걸쳐 날짜가 적힌 메모(오랜 반복 독서)를 보여 주고, 그 메모가 Lucien이 추천한 구절에 대한 응답(Lucien과의 연결)임을 보여 주므로 두 조건을 모두 충족한다. A는 Lucien이 자신의 오해를 깨닫는다는 내용이지만, 책의 상태가 무엇을 뜻하는지는 설명하지 못한다. B는 오히려 선물을 모욕으로 본 Lucien의 해석에 배경을 줄 뿐이다. C는 책의 내력을 알려 주지만 Lucien과 무관한 곳에서 산 책이므로 헌신이 Lucien과 연결된다는 점을 뒷받침하지 못한다.
input.explanation_en: Marchetti's argument has two parts: the book's worn condition is evidence of devotion Aubert built up over many years, and that devotion is tied directly to Lucien. D satisfies both. Notes dated across many years show long, repeated reading, and the fact that they respond to passages Lucien recommended links the wear to Lucien himself. A shows that Lucien realizes he was wrong, but it says nothing about what the book's condition means. B only gives background for Lucien's view that the gift was an insult. C tells you where the book came from, but because Aubert bought it somewhere unrelated to Lucien, it actually fails to connect the book to him.
input.design: 이 문항은 정답이 주장의 두 요소(오랜 세월의 헌신과 Lucien과의 연결)를 모두 충족해야 하도록 설계했다. A(오해를 깨달음)와 C(책의 내력)는 각각 일부만 맞는 오답이다. 네 선택지는 모두 'In a later chapter, Lucien...'이라는 같은 문장 틀로 썼고, 질문에는 정답의 핵심어를 넣지 않았다.

input.passage: When a liquid is blasted with intense sound waves, tiny gas bubbles form, swell, and then collapse violently, a process called acoustic cavitation. In 1990, physicist Felipe Gaitan found a way to trap a single bubble at the center of a flask of water, where it expanded and collapsed tens of thousands of times per second, giving off a faint flash of blue light with every collapse. This effect, known as sonoluminescence, had been seen in clouds of bubbles since the 1930s, but isolating one bubble let researchers measure it precisely. They found that each flash lasts less than a billionth of a second and that the gas inside the bubble may reach thousands of degrees as the bubble shrinks. Still, how the light is actually produced is debated. Some researchers credit heating from shock waves converging inside the bubble, while others argue that the hot gas simply glows the way any very hot material does, and so far no experiment has clearly ruled out either explanation.
input.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Gaitan's single-bubble experiment showed that sonoluminescence is caused by shock waves converging inside a collapsing bubble.
Trapping a single bubble allowed sonoluminescence to be studied in detail, but the process that creates its light is still unresolved.
Trapping a single bubble showed that sonoluminescence flashes are far hotter and briefer than flashes produced by clouds of bubbles.
Trapping a single bubble allowed researchers to observe sonoluminescence for the first time after decades of failed attempts.
input.explanation: 지문은 단일 기포를 가두는 방법 덕분에 소노루미네선스를 정밀하게 측정할 수 있게 되었지만, 빛이 생기는 원리는 여전히 논쟁 중이라고 말하므로 B가 정답이다. A는 여러 가설 중 하나인 충격파를 확정된 결론처럼 말하지만, 지문은 어느 설명도 배제되지 않았다고 한다. C는 지문에 나온 수치를 활용하지만 기포 무리에서 나는 빛과 비교한 내용은 지문에 없다. D는 이 현상이 1930년대부터 이미 관찰되었다는 사실과 어긋난다.
input.explanation_en: The text says that isolating one bubble let researchers measure sonoluminescence precisely, but scientists still argue over how the light is produced, so B is correct. A treats one competing hypothesis, shock waves, as proven, while the text says neither explanation has been ruled out. C uses details from the measurements, but the text never compares single-bubble flashes with flashes from bubble clouds. D contradicts the text, which says the effect had already been seen in clouds of bubbles since the 1930s.
input.design: 세 오답 모두 정답과 같은 'Trapping a single bubble…' 문장 틀을 쓰고, 지문의 실제 세부 내용(충격파 가설, 측정 수치, 1930년대)을 잘못 활용하게 만들었다. 그래서 마지막 문장의 '아직 풀리지 않음'과 앞부분의 진전을 함께 연결해야 정답을 고를 수 있다.

input.passage: In petroleum refining, catalytic cracking breaks long hydrocarbon chains into the smaller molecules that make up gasoline. Many refineries rely on zeolites, crystalline aluminosilicates riddled with pores less than a nanometer wide, to speed this process. Because reactions occur mainly inside these micropores, the pore dimensions determine which molecules can enter, which transition states can form, and which products can escape. __One might therefore expect that the zeolite with the widest pores would always be preferred, since it admits the greatest variety of feedstock molecules.__ Yet engineers often favor zeolites with narrower channels: by excluding bulky branched molecules and preventing the formation of large intermediates that tend to produce coke, these tighter pores yield a more predictable product mixture and extend the catalyst's working life.
input.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It presents a seemingly reasonable assumption that the text then shows to be incomplete.
It presents a finding that the text then uses to explain how coke forms inside zeolites.
It presents a conclusion that the text then supports with evidence about catalyst lifespan.
It presents a definition that the text then applies to the selection of refinery feedstocks.
input.explanation: 밑줄 문장은 'One might therefore expect'로 시작하여, 기공 크기가 중요하다는 앞 내용에서 자연스럽게 나올 법한 예상(가장 넓은 기공이 최선)을 제시하고, 바로 다음 'Yet' 문장이 더 좁은 기공이 선호되는 이유를 들어 그 예상이 불충분함을 보여 준다. 따라서 A가 정답이다. B는 코크 형성이 뒤에 언급되기는 하지만 밑줄 문장은 연구 결과가 아니라 가정이며 코크 설명의 근거로 쓰이지 않는다. C는 촉매 수명이 뒤에 나오지만 그것은 밑줄 문장을 뒷받침하는 것이 아니라 반박한다. D는 밑줄 문장이 정의가 아니고, 글은 원료 선택이 아니라 촉매 선택을 다룬다.
input.explanation_en: The underlined sentence begins with "One might therefore expect," which offers a prediction that seems to follow from the earlier point about pore size: the widest pores should always be best. The next sentence opens with "Yet" and explains why narrower pores are often chosen, which shows that the expectation is incomplete. That makes A the answer. B doesn't work because the sentence is an assumption, not a finding, and it isn't used to explain how coke forms, even though coke comes up later. C doesn't work because the point about catalyst lifespan argues against the underlined sentence instead of supporting it. D doesn't work because the sentence isn't a definition, and the text is about choosing a catalyst, not choosing feedstocks.
input.design: Wrong answers B and C borrow details that appear later in the text (coke, catalyst lifespan) but get the logical relationship wrong. A student skimming the text could miss that "Yet" overturns the expectation in the underlined sentence. All four options use the same "It presents X that the text then..." frame.

input.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- "The Dented Bell" is a 2019 short story by the German writer Lena Haubrich.
- The story is set in a small Bavarian village, at a weekly rehearsal of the local brass band.

input.question: The student wants to describe the surprising event at the center of the story. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: In Lena Haubrich's 2019 short story "The Dented Bell," a brass band in a small Bavarian village holds its weekly rehearsal.
In Lena Haubrich's short story "The Dented Bell," Anton's tuba, damaged in a fall from his bicycle, produces a softer and warmer tone than the band has ever heard.
In Lena Haubrich's short story "The Dented Bell," which was translated into English in 2022, the main character is an elderly tuba player named Anton.

input.explanation: 목표는 이야기 중심의 놀라운 사건을 묘사하는 것이다. B는 망가진 튜바가 오히려 밴드가 들어 본 적 없는 부드럽고 따뜻한 소리를 낸다는 점을 전해 목표에 맞는다. A는 배경(마을, 연습)만 소개하고 놀라운 사건이 없다. C는 번역 연도와 주인공 소개일 뿐 사건을 다루지 않는다. D는 튜바가 수리되어 예전과 같은 소리를 낸다고 해 메모 내용과 어긋나는 부정확한 진술이다.
input.explanation_en: Your goal is to describe the surprising event at the heart of the story. B does this: it explains that Anton's tuba, damaged in a fall, makes a softer and warmer tone than the band has ever heard. A only gives the setting (the village and the rehearsal) and doesn't mention anything surprising. C tells you the translation date and introduces the main character, but it doesn't describe an event. D is inaccurate, because the notes never say the tuba is repaired or that it sounds the same as before.
input.design: 목표가 메모 4~5번에 직접 대응하는 한 단계 문제로, 오답은 배경·서지 메모 사용 및 메모와 어긋나는 진술로 구성했다. 같은 문장 틀을 유지했고, 질문에는 정답의 핵심어(damaged, warmer tone)를 쓰지 않았다.

content.text:
Notes about a fictional story; goal e.g., emphasize the contrast between Desta's plan and the interruption... Must avoid wording overlap. Let's design.

Notes:
- "The Third Cup" is a 2019 short story by Ethiopian writer Hirut Bekele (fictional).
- In it, Desta hosts a coffee ceremony, roasting beans for her family in Addis Ababa.
- She has secretly bought a one-way ticket to Toronto and plans to tell her family after the first cup is poured.
- Before the first cup, Almaz, a woman Desta has not seen since leaving her childhood village, knocks at the door.
- Almaz was the one who taught Desta to roast coffee when Desta was a girl.
- Desta pours the third cup, the baraka (blessing), without having made her announcement.

Goal: emphasize how the guest's arrival disrupts Desta's plan. Question wording should avoid "interrupt". Phrase: "The student wants to explain the timing of the visitor's appearance in relation to Desta's intentions."

Correct A: "Desta intends to reveal her one-way ticket to Toronto once the first cup is poured, but before that moment arrives, Almaz, a woman from her childhood village, knocks at the door."
B: focuses on Almaz teaching roasting — same frame.
C: ceremony ending with the third cup, no announcement — partial but doesn't mention the arrival timing/plan... Actually mentions no announcement; omits guest. Good.
D: story intro.

input.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- "The Third Cup" is a 2019 short story by the fictional Ethiopian writer Hirut Bekele.
- In the story, Desta hosts a traditional coffee ceremony for her family in Addis Ababa, roasting the green beans herself.
- Desta has secretly bought a one-way ticket to Toronto and plans to tell her family once the first cup is poured.
- Before the first cup is served, Almaz, a woman Desta has not seen since leaving her childhood village, knocks at the door.
- Almaz was the person who taught Desta to roast coffee when Desta was a girl.
- By the time Desta pours the third cup, known as the baraka, or blessing, she still has not shared her news.
input.question: The student wants to explain how the visitor's appearance relates to the timing of Desta's intentions. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: Desta plans to reveal her one-way ticket to Toronto as soon as the first cup is poured, but before that moment comes, Almaz, a woman from her childhood village, knocks at the door.
Desta roasts the green beans herself for the ceremony, a skill she learned as a girl from Almaz, a woman from her childhood village who later knocks at the door.
Desta plans to reveal her one-way ticket to Toronto during the ceremony, but even after the third cup, the baraka, is poured, she has not shared her news.
Desta hosts a traditional coffee ceremony for her family in Addis Ababa in "The Third Cup," a 2019 short story by Hirut Bekele.
input.explanation: 목표는 손님의 등장이 데스타의 계획 시점과 어떻게 맞물리는지 설명하는 것이다. A는 첫 잔을 따른 뒤 알리려던 계획과, 그 순간이 오기 전에 알마즈가 문을 두드리는 장면을 함께 보여 주어 목표를 이룬다. B는 알마즈와 데스타의 과거 인연을 강조할 뿐 데스타의 계획은 다루지 않는다. C는 계획과 그 계획이 실현되지 않은 결과를 말하지만 손님의 등장을 빠뜨려 둘 사이의 관계를 보여 주지 못한다. D는 작품과 배경을 소개할 뿐 계획도 손님도 언급하지 않는다.
input.explanation_en: Your goal is to show how the visitor's arrival lines up with the timing of Desta's plan. Choice A does this: it states that Desta meant to make her announcement after the first cup and that Almaz knocks before that moment comes. Choice B focuses on Desta's past connection to Almaz but never mentions Desta's plan. Choice C gives the plan and the fact that it doesn't happen, but it leaves out the visitor, so it can't show how her arrival relates to the plan. Choice D only introduces the story and its setting.
input.design: 정답은 계획 메모와 손님 도착 메모를 시간적으로 연결해야 하며, C는 계획+미실현 결과로 그럴듯하지만 손님이 빠지고, B는 손님을 다루지만 계획이 빠져 비교가 필요하다.

content.text: Design: a concession followed by a reversal, with no word in the passage that hints at the relationship. Deepak's family assumes he will open the box. He does lift the latch, but then he closes it again without looking inside. The right transition is "Instead," and the distractors are "Moreover," "As a result," and "For instance."

input.passage: On the houseboat drifting through the Kerala backwaters, Deepak turned his grandmother's sandalwood box over in his hands. His aunts had made it clear that they expected him to open it that evening, and he had even pressed his thumb against the brass latch until it gave a small click. ______ he set the box on the shelf beside her old prayer lamp, the latch closed again, deciding that whatever she had kept inside could stay hers a little longer.
input.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
options: Moreover,
As a result,
Instead,
For instance,
input.explanation: 앞 문장은 가족의 기대와 걸쇠를 누른 행동으로 상자를 열 것 같은 방향을 제시하고, 빈칸 뒤에서는 상자를 닫은 채 선반에 두기로 한다. 예상된 행동 대신 다른 행동을 택한 것이므로 대안·반전을 나타내는 C가 정답이다. A는 같은 방향의 정보를 덧붙이는 표현인데, 뒤 문장은 앞의 흐름을 뒤집는다. B는 걸쇠를 누른 것이 상자를 닫아 두는 결과로 이어진 것처럼 만들어 인과 방향이 맞지 않는다. D는 뒤 문장을 앞 내용의 예시로 만들지만, 상자를 열지 않는 것은 열려는 기대의 예가 아니다.
input.explanation_en: The earlier sentence leans toward opening the box: his aunts expect it, and Deepak even clicks the latch. The next sentence goes the other way, because he puts the box away still closed. He chooses a different action from the one that was expected, so the reversal word in C fits. A adds information that continues in the same direction, but this sentence reverses the earlier one. B treats closing the box as a result of pressing the latch, which gets the cause and effect wrong. D presents the sentence as an example, but leaving the box closed is not an example of the expectation that he would open it.
input.design: This tests a concession followed by a reversal with no signal word in the passage. A quick read of "even pressed the latch" might pull a student toward B (result) or A (adding on).

input.passage:
The following text is adapted from a short story about two neighbors in a small Texas town on the border.

By the middle of August the heat had flattened Louise's tomatoes and turned Hector's roses to paper, but the watermelons kept swelling. Every evening at seven, Hector walked to the chain-link fence with his tape measure, and every evening Louise was already waiting there with hers. They announced their numbers like auctioneers. Hector had begun shading his melon with a beach umbrella; Louise had answered by playing it radio stations from Monterrey. Neither one mentioned that the rest of the street had gone quiet, that the Garzas had moved in with their daughter and old Mr. Peña no longer came out at all.

A literary critic argues that the story presents the watermelon contest not mainly as a rivalry but as an excuse that lets the two aging neighbors keep up a daily connection while the heat isolates everyone around them.
input.question: Which finding, if true, would most directly support the critic's interpretation?
options: Later in the story, Hector tells customers at the hardware store that his melon is already heavier than any Louise has grown.
Later in the story, Louise begins watering her melon after midnight so that Hector cannot see the fertilizer she mixes in.
Later in the story, after Louise's melon splits open and she can no longer win, Hector still comes to the fence every evening at seven to compare vines with her.
Later in the story, the owner of the local seed store mentions that Hector and Louise have bought the same variety of watermelon seed for many years.
input.design: 두 단계 판단을 요구한다. 먼저 비평가의 주장이 '경쟁보다 매일의 만남이 핵심'이라는 점을 파악하고, 다음으로 경쟁이 사라진 뒤에도 만남이 계속되는지를 확인해야 한다. 오답은 모두 같은 'Later in the story' 문장 틀을 쓰며, 두 사람의 관계나 경쟁을 그럴듯하게 다룬다.
input.explanation: 비평가는 수박 경쟁이 진짜 경쟁이라기보다 두 이웃이 매일 만나기 위한 핑계라고 주장한다. C에서는 루이즈가 이길 가능성이 사라져 경쟁의 의미가 없어졌는데도 헥터가 매일 저녁 울타리로 찾아온다. 이는 두 사람을 이어 주는 것이 승부가 아니라 만남 자체임을 보여 주므로 주장을 가장 직접적으로 뒷받침한다. A와 B는 자랑하고 몰래 비료를 쓰는 모습을 보여 주어 오히려 진짜 경쟁이라는 해석을 강화한다. D는 두 사람의 오랜 공통점을 보여 주지만, 더위 속 고립에 맞서 매일 관계를 이어 간다는 점과는 관련이 없다.
input.explanation_en: The critic claims the contest is really an excuse that keeps the two neighbors in daily contact, not mainly a rivalry. In C, Louise can no longer win, so the competition has lost its point, yet Hector keeps coming to the fence every evening. That shows the meeting itself is what matters, so C supports the claim most directly. A and B show bragging and secret fertilizing, which makes the rivalry look real and works against the critic's reading. D shows a long-standing similarity between the two, but it says nothing about them keeping up daily contact while the heat isolates everyone else.

input.passage: Every morning the school boat left Tagbac before the tide turned, and the children, crowded beneath its patched blue canopy, made up games to fill the hour. The newest game, invented by Lorna Dimaculangan, a quiet girl who swore she had dreamed it during the last typhoon______ that anyone walking between the island's villages at midday must never once step on his or her own shadow. By the time the boat reached the pier, even the boatman was squinting at the sun and planning his route home.
input.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: , required
required
; required
—required
input.design: 긴 분사구와 동격 명사구가 주어와 동사 사이에 끼어 있어서, 학생은 동격구가 쉼표로 시작했다는 점을 확인하고 같은 부호로 닫아야 한다는 것을 판단해야 한다. 대시는 동격구를 닫는 역할로 그럴듯해 보이지만 여는 부호와 짝이 맞지 않는다.
input.explanation: 이 문장의 주어는 "The newest game"이고 동사는 "required"이다. 그 사이에 "invented by ..."라는 수식어와 "a quiet girl who ... typhoon"이라는 동격구가 끼어 있다. 동격구가 쉼표로 시작했으므로 같은 쉼표로 닫아야 하고, 그래서 A가 정답이다. B는 닫는 쉼표가 없어서 "typhoon required"가 관계절 속 동사처럼 읽혀 버린다. C의 세미콜론은 주어와 동사를 갈라놓아 앞부분이 독립절이 되지 못한다. D의 대시는 쉼표로 연 삽입구를 다른 부호로 닫는 것이라 짝이 맞지 않는다.
input.explanation_en: The subject of this sentence is "The newest game," and its verb is "required." Between them sit the modifier "invented by ..." and the appositive "a quiet girl who ... typhoon." That appositive opens with a comma, so it has to close with a comma too, and that makes A correct. B leaves out the closing comma, so "typhoon required" reads as if the verb belonged inside the "who" clause. C puts a semicolon between the subject and its verb, and that's a problem because the words before a semicolon must form an independent clause, which they don't here. D closes with a dash even though the interruption opened with a comma, so the punctuation doesn't match.

content.text:
Literary fiction scene. Test: dangling modifier or finite verb vs participle. Let's do subject-verb agreement after long modifier with tricky noun.

Passage: "Every morning at 7:40, the Johnsons descended from their third-floor apartment to the Garfield Boulevard platform in the same order: Mr. Johnson first, then his wife, then nine-year-old Della. On the Tuesday the dog appeared—a gaunt brown shepherd mix curled beneath the bench—that order collapsed. Della knelt beside the animal, and the routine of the household, built over years of punctual trains and pressed shirts, ______ apart in a single refusal to stand up."

Options: "were coming", "having come", "to come", "came". Need two-step: subject "routine" singular (distractor "were coming" plural agrees with shirts/trains), finite verb needed after "and" clause. "having come"/"to come" non-finite. Also maybe "coming". Fine.

input.passage: Every weekday at 7:40, the Johnsons climbed to the Garfield Boulevard platform in the same order: Mr. Johnson first, then his wife, then nine-year-old Della with her lunch pail. But on the cold Tuesday that a gaunt brown dog appeared beneath the platform bench, ribs showing through its matted coat, Della knelt beside it and would not move. As the southbound train rattled in and out without them, the routine of the household, built over years of punctual departures and carefully pressed shirts, ______ apart in a single stubborn refusal to stand up.
input.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: were coming
having come
to come
came
input.explanation: 이 절의 주어는 단수 명사 'the routine'이고, 삽입된 수식어구 'built over years of ... shirts' 다음에 정동사가 와야 절이 완성된다. D의 'came'은 단수 주어와 맞는 정동사이며, 앞 문장들의 과거 시제와도 일치한다. A의 'were coming'은 정동사이긴 하지만 수식어구 안의 복수 명사(departures, shirts)에 맞춘 복수형이라 단수 주어 'routine'과 일치하지 않는다. B의 'having come'과 C의 'to come'은 비정형(분사·부정사)이어서 주어 'routine'에 정동사가 없게 되므로 문장이 성립하지 않는다.
input.explanation_en: The subject of this clause is the singular noun "the routine," and after the modifier "built over years of ... shirts," the clause still needs a main verb to be complete. Choice D, "came," is a main verb that agrees with the singular subject and also fits the past tense used in the rest of the passage. Choice A, "were coming," is a main verb, but it's plural: it agrees with the nouns inside the modifier ("departures," "shirts"), not with the singular subject "routine." Choices B ("having come") and C ("to come") are nonfinite forms (a participle and an infinitive), so "routine" would be left with no main verb and the sentence wouldn't work.
input.design: To get this right, students have to look past a long modifier with plural nouns, find the singular subject, and then see that the clause needs a main verb. One wrong answer has the right structure but the wrong number, and two have the right meaning but aren't main verbs.

input.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- "The Borrowed Net" is a 2016 short story by Egyptian writer Nadia Fawzy.
- The story is set on a rooftop in Cairo's Shubra district, where many residents keep pigeon lofts.
- The narrator, Hassan, lends his favorite pigeon-catching net to his childhood friend Karim.
- Hassan watches from the rooftop as Karim carries the net into the crowded streets below; Karim never returns it.
- By the story's last page, Hassan and Karim have stopped speaking to each other.
- Critics have noted that Fawzy uses the lost net to stand for the fading bond between the two boys.
input.question: The student wants to explain what the lending episode means within the story as a whole. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: In Fawzy's "The Borrowed Net," Hassan lends his net on a Shubra rooftop, a neighborhood where many Cairo residents keep pigeon lofts.
In Fawzy's "The Borrowed Net," Hassan lends his favorite net to Karim, who carries it into the crowded streets and never returns it.
In Fawzy's "The Borrowed Net," the net Hassan watches disappear with Karim into Cairo's streets comes to represent the friendship that quietly dissolves between them.
In Fawzy's "The Borrowed Net," a 2016 story by an Egyptian writer, Hassan lends a pigeon-catching net to his childhood friend Karim.
input.design: 정답은 빌려준 장면(메모 4)과 비평가의 상징 해석·관계 단절(메모 5·6)을 묶어야 한다. 오답 B와 D는 같은 장면을 정확하게 옮기지만 그 장면이 무엇을 뜻하는지는 말하지 않는다. A는 배경 정보에 머문다. 네 선택지는 모두 같은 문장 틀을 쓴다.
input.explanation: 목표는 그물을 빌려준 일이 이야기 전체에서 어떤 의미를 갖는지 설명하는 것이다. C는 그물이 거리로 사라지는 장면과, 그물이 두 소년의 우정을 상징한다는 비평가의 해석을 연결한다. 그래서 정답이다. A는 배경인 슈브라 지역의 비둘기 사육장만 언급할 뿐 의미는 다루지 않는다. B는 줄거리를 정확하게 요약하지만 그 사건이 무엇을 상징하는지 설명하지 않는다. D는 작가와 출간 연도 같은 기본 정보와 사건만 소개하므로 목표에서 벗어난다.
input.explanation_en: Your goal is to explain what lending the net means within the story as a whole. C does this by linking the net vanishing into the streets to the critics' reading that the net represents the boys' fading friendship. A only describes the setting, the pigeon lofts of Shubra, and never addresses meaning. B accurately retells the plot but never says what the event stands for. D just introduces the author, the date, and the basic event, so it also misses the goal.

input.passage: Three-toed sloths descend from the forest canopy about once a week to defecate at the base of their trees, a trip that exposes them to predators and burns precious energy. Ecologist Jonathan Pauli and colleagues proposed that the habit is tied to moths living in the sloths' fur: female moths leave the sloth during these descents to lay eggs in the dung, and the emerging adults fly up to colonize sloths in the canopy. The moths, in turn, appear to deposit nitrogen and other nutrients into the fur, fueling the growth of algae there. __Notably, the researchers found that sloths carrying more moths also had higher concentrations of inorganic nitrogen and greater algal biomass in their fur.__ Because sloths have been observed licking algae from their coats, and because the algae are rich in digestible carbohydrates and lipids, the team suggested that this greenish growth may supplement the sloths' notoriously low-nutrient diet of leaves, in addition to helping camouflage them among the foliage.
input.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It presents a finding that challenges the claim that sloths descend from the canopy in order to aid the moths' reproduction.
It provides evidence for a proposed link between the moths and algal growth that the text goes on to connect to a possible benefit for sloths.
It introduces a finding that explains why sloths choose to defecate at the base of their trees rather than in the canopy.
It offers an observation suggesting that algae, rather than moths, are the main source of nitrogen in sloths' fur.
input.explanation: 밑줄 문장은 나방이 많을수록 털 속 질소와 조류가 많다는 결과로, 바로 앞 문장의 '나방이 영양분을 공급해 조류 성장을 돕는다'는 주장을 뒷받침하고, 이후 문장은 이 조류가 나무늘보의 영양·위장에 도움이 될 수 있다고 연결하므로 B가 정답이다. A는 이 결과가 연구진의 가설을 반박하는 것이 아니라 오히려 지지한다는 점에서 틀렸다. C는 나무늘보의 하강 행동이 지문에서 다뤄지긴 하지만, 밑줄 문장은 하강의 이유가 아니라 털 속 성분을 다룬다. D는 질소의 원천을 거꾸로 서술하고 있는데, 지문은 나방이 영양분을 공급한다고 말한다.
input.explanation_en: The underlined sentence reports that sloths with more moths had more nitrogen and algae in their fur. This backs up the previous sentence's claim that moths supply nutrients that help algae grow, and the next sentence then ties those algae to possible nutrition and camouflage benefits for sloths, so B is correct. A is wrong because the finding supports the researchers' hypothesis instead of challenging it. C is wrong because the text does discuss the descents, but the underlined sentence is about what is in the fur, not about why sloths come down to defecate. D reverses the source of the nitrogen, since the text says the moths supply the nutrients.
input.design: 세 오답 모두 지문에 나오는 요소(하강, 번식, 질소)를 활용해 일부는 맞아 보이게 만들었다. 정답을 고르려면 밑줄 문장을 앞 문장의 주장, 뒤 문장의 결론과 함께 연결해 읽어야 한다.

input.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- Photocatalytic water splitting uses light energy to break water molecules into hydrogen and oxygen gas.
- In 1972, Japanese researchers Akira Fujishima and Kenichi Honda showed that titanium dioxide (TiO2) could split water when exposed to ultraviolet light.
- TiO2 is inexpensive, nontoxic, and resists corrosion in water, so it can be used for long periods.
- However, TiO2 absorbs only ultraviolet light, which makes up about 4 percent of the energy in sunlight.
- Because of this, TiO2 systems running on ordinary sunlight convert only a small fraction of incoming solar energy into hydrogen.
input.question: The student wants to present both an advantage and a drawback of using titanium dioxide for this process. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: Titanium dioxide is inexpensive and nontoxic, and in 1972 Fujishima and Honda showed that it could split water into hydrogen and oxygen under ultraviolet light.
Titanium dioxide is inexpensive and resists corrosion in water, but because it absorbs only ultraviolet light, it converts just a small fraction of sunlight's energy into hydrogen.
Titanium dioxide absorbs only ultraviolet light, which makes up about 4 percent of sunlight's energy, so it converts just a small fraction of incoming solar energy into hydrogen.
Titanium dioxide uses light energy to break water into hydrogen and oxygen, and it resists corrosion in water, so it can be used for long periods.
input.explanation: 정답은 B이다. B는 저렴하고 부식에 강하다는 장점과, 자외선만 흡수해 태양에너지의 일부만 수소로 바꾼다는 단점을 'but'으로 함께 제시한다. A와 D는 정확한 메모를 쓰지만 장점이나 일반적 사실만 담고 단점이 없다. C는 단점을 원인과 결과까지 자세히 설명하지만 장점이 빠져 있어 목표의 절반만 달성한다.
input.explanation_en: The answer is B. Choice B gives an advantage (TiO2 is inexpensive and resists corrosion) and a drawback (it absorbs only ultraviolet light, so it converts little of sunlight's energy into hydrogen), linking the two with "but." Choices A and D use accurate notes, but they give only advantages or general facts, with no drawback. Choice C explains the drawback carefully, cause and effect included, but it leaves out any advantage, so it meets only half of the goal.
input.design: 질문은 '장점과 단점'이라는 추상어만 쓰고 정답 문구를 반복하지 않았다. 오답 셋도 정답과 같은 'Titanium dioxide…' 문장 틀이다. C는 단점만, A·D는 장점만 담아서 메모 두 가지를 결합해야만 정답을 고를 수 있다.

input.passage: When engineers first examined carbon-fiber laminates that had failed under repeated bending, they assumed the cracks between layers had begun in the resin itself. Microscopy by materials scientist Lena Okafor complicated that view: the earliest damage appeared not within the resin but along the thin boundary where resin meets fiber, and only after these tiny separations joined together did a visible crack spread between plies. Okafor's findings thus ______ the earlier assumption, showing that it described a later stage of failure rather than its origin.
input.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
options: qualified
confirmed
overturned
anticipated
input.explanation: 지문은 Okafor의 연구가 기존 가정을 "복잡하게 했다"고 하고, 그 가정이 틀린 것이 아니라 파손의 기원이 아닌 후기 단계를 설명한다고 보여 주었다고 한다. 따라서 가정을 부분적으로 제한·수정했다는 뜻의 A(qualified)가 가장 정확하다. B는 연구가 가정을 그대로 지지한다는 뜻이어서 기원이 다르다는 발견과 맞지 않는다. C는 '완전히 뒤집었다'는 뜻인데, 지문은 가정이 후기 단계에 대해서는 여전히 유효하다고 하므로 너무 강하다. D는 연구가 가정보다 먼저 나왔다는 뜻이 되어 시간 순서와 맞지 않는다.
input.explanation_en: The text says Okafor's microscopy "complicated" the earlier view and showed that the assumption described a later stage of failure instead of its origin. So her findings limited or refined the assumption without throwing it out, and that is what A ("qualified") means. B doesn't work because the findings did not simply support the assumption, since they located the origin somewhere else. C goes too far: "overturned" means rejecting the assumption completely, but the text says it still holds for the later crack stage. D would mean the findings came before the assumption, which reverses the order of events.
input.design: 'overturned'는 반박이라는 점에서 일부 맞고, 'confirmed'는 균열이 실제로 층간에 퍼진다는 점에서 일부 맞다. 따라서 마지막 절을 정독해야 '부분 수정'이라는 뉘앙스를 가려낼 수 있다.

input.passage: On the night of his final concert with the Bavarian brass band, Ernst lifted the trumpet his grandfather had repaired decades earlier. He ran his thumb along the bell, feeling each small hollow in the brass. The dents on the old instrument ______ reminders of stories that no one in the band could remember anymore, yet Ernst felt them all as he raised the trumpet to play.
input.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: was
is
were
has been
input.explanation: 이 문장의 주어는 복수 명사 "The dents"이며, "on the old instrument"는 주어를 꾸미는 전치사구일 뿐이다. 또한 이야기가 과거 시제(lifted, ran, felt)로 서술되므로 복수 과거형 동사가 필요하다. 따라서 C "were"가 정답이다. A "was"와 D "has been"은 단수 동사여서 수가 맞지 않으며, 바로 앞의 단수 명사 "instrument"에 이끌려 고르기 쉬운 오답이다. B "is"는 단수인 데다 현재 시제라서 수와 시제가 모두 맞지 않는다.
input.explanation_en: The subject of this sentence is the plural noun "The dents." The phrase "on the old instrument" only describes the subject. The story is also told in the past tense (lifted, ran, felt), so you need a plural past-tense verb. That makes C, "were," the correct answer. A ("was") and D ("has been") are singular verbs, so they don't agree with the subject. They're easy to pick by mistake because the singular noun "instrument" comes right before the blank. B ("is") is wrong on both counts: it's singular, and it's in the present tense.
input.design: 짧은 전치사구가 낀 주어-동사 수 일치라는 단일 규칙을 묻고, 바로 앞 단수 명사로 인한 전형적 오개념을 오답으로 배치했다.

input.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- "The Extra Bowl" is a short story by a Vietnamese American writer.
- It is set in a street-food alley in Hanoi at dawn.
- Its main character is Tuan, a seven-year-old boy who helps at his aunt's noodle stall.
- Every morning, an old man orders two bowls of soup but eats only one.
- Tuan finally asks the adults why no one seems to notice the untouched bowl.
input.question: The student wants to tell readers who the main character of the story is and where the story takes place. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: "The Extra Bowl" is a short story by a Vietnamese American writer about an old man who orders two bowls of soup.
In "The Extra Bowl," an old man orders two bowls of soup every morning but eats only one of them.
"The Extra Bowl" follows Tuan, a seven-year-old boy who helps at a noodle stall in a Hanoi street-food alley at dawn.
In "The Extra Bowl," a boy finally asks the adults why no one notices a bowl of soup that is never eaten.
input.explanation: 목표는 주인공이 누구인지와 이야기의 배경을 함께 밝히는 것이다. C는 주인공(일곱 살 소년 Tuan)과 배경(새벽의 하노이 길거리 음식 골목)을 모두 담고 있다. A는 작가와 노인 손님 이야기만 하고 주인공과 배경은 빠져 있다. B는 노인의 행동만 설명하며 주인공도 배경도 나오지 않는다. D는 소년의 질문을 언급하지만 이름도 배경도 밝히지 않는다.
input.explanation_en: Your goal is to say who the main character is and where the story takes place. C does both: it names Tuan, a seven-year-old boy, and places the story in a Hanoi street-food alley at dawn. A gives the author and the old customer but leaves out the main character and the setting. B only describes what the old man does, so it has neither the main character nor the setting. D mentions a boy's question but doesn't give his name or say where the story happens.
input.design: 목표가 주인공·배경 두 메모와 직접 대응하고, 오답은 같은 문장 틀로 줄거리·작가 등 목표와 무관한 메모를 활용하게 했다.

input.passage: Conventional microfluidic chips move fluids through networks of fixed channels, so each chip is effectively built for a single assay. Digital microfluidic devices take a different approach: they move discrete droplets across a grid of electrodes using electrowetting, in which an applied voltage changes how strongly a droplet wets the surface beneath it, pulling the droplet toward the energized electrode. __Because the path a droplet follows is set by the sequence of electrodes switched on rather than by etched channels, the same chip can be reprogrammed to split, merge, or route droplets for an entirely different experiment.__ Engineer Aaron Wheeler and colleagues have used this flexibility to isolate individual cells in separate droplets, expose each one to a different reagent, and then measure the cells' responses one at a time, an analysis that would have required several purpose-built channel chips.
input.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It describes the physical mechanism by which an applied voltage causes a droplet to move toward an energized electrode.
It identifies a consequence of the way droplets are controlled that makes possible the single-cell work described afterward.
It presents a limitation of channel-based chips that Wheeler's team set out to overcome by isolating cells in droplets.
It offers evidence from Wheeler's experiments that digital devices measure cell responses more accurately than channel chips do.
input.explanation: 밑줄 문장은 앞 문장에서 설명한 전극 기반 제어 방식의 결과로 칩을 재프로그래밍할 수 있다는 점을 제시하고, 이 '유연성'이 다음 문장의 단일 세포 분석을 가능하게 하므로 B가 정답이다. A의 전압·젖음 메커니즘은 밑줄 문장이 아니라 바로 앞 문장의 내용이다. C는 채널 칩의 한계를 다루는 것처럼 보이지만, 밑줄 문장은 디지털 장치의 장점을 말하며 Wheeler 팀의 동기도 언급하지 않는다. D는 지문에 없는 '정확도' 비교를 주장하며, 밑줄 문장은 실험 증거도 아니다.
input.explanation_en: The underlined sentence explains what follows from controlling droplets with electrodes: the chip can be reprogrammed. The next sentence then calls this "flexibility" and shows it making single-cell analysis possible, so B is correct. A describes the voltage-and-wetting mechanism, but that comes in the sentence before the underlined one. C may look right because channel chips come up, but the underlined sentence describes an advantage of digital devices, and the text never says what motivated Wheeler's team. D is wrong because the text never compares accuracy, and the underlined sentence isn't experimental evidence.
input.design: To answer, students have to connect the underlined sentence to both the sentence before it (the mechanism) and the sentence after it (the application). Each wrong answer is tempting for a reason: A uses the mechanism from the sentence before, C picks up the contrast with channel chips, and D borrows Wheeler's experiments.

input.passage: For three weeks, Elsa had moved between the apartments of the boarding house on Gumpendorfer Strasse, coaxing the Hungarian widow on the second floor and the silent Silesian brothers in the attic to sing together at the Easter service. By the final rehearsal, the hymn finally held its shape, and even Herr Brandl, who rarely left his room, tapped his cane in time. ______ when the widow corrected the elder brother's pronunciation of a single word, he set down his hymnal, walked out of the stairwell, and did not return, taking his brother with him.
input.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
options: Consequently,
Even so,
Specifically,
In the same way,
input.explanation: 앞 문장은 리허설이 마침내 잘 맞아떨어지고 은둔하던 브란들 씨까지 박자를 맞췄다는 화합의 모습을 보여 준다. 뒷 문장은 사소한 지적 하나로 형제가 자리를 떠나 버리는 정반대의 결말이므로, 앞의 진전에도 불구하고 평화가 깨졌음을 나타내는 B가 정답이다. A는 화합이 이탈의 원인이었다는 뜻이 되지만, 실제 원인은 발음 지적이다. C는 뒷 문장이 앞 내용을 구체화한다는 뜻인데, 형제의 이탈은 화합의 예시가 아니라 그 반대이다. D는 두 장면이 비슷하다는 뜻이 되지만 두 장면은 서로 대조된다.
input.explanation_en: The first sentences show the rehearsal finally going well, with even the reclusive Herr Brandl keeping time. The next sentence shows the opposite: one small correction makes the brothers walk out. B fits because it signals that the peace broke down despite all that progress. A says the harmony caused the walkout, but the real trigger is the pronunciation correction. C would mean the walkout is a specific example of the harmony, when it actually contradicts it. D says the two moments are alike, but they are clearly contrasted.
input.design: 빈칸 앞뒤에 대조를 알려 주는 단어가 없어서, 화합에서 결렬로 흐름이 바뀐다는 것을 직접 파악해야 한다. A는 앞뒤 사건이 시간 순서로 이어져 보여서 고르기 쉽고, C는 뒷문장이 구체적인 일화라서 그럴듯해 보인다.

input.passage: Halfway across the channel, the old fisherman spread the torn sail over his knees and motioned for Iris to sit beside him. He spoke slowly, as if each instruction might be the last he would ever give. The rhythm of his hands, pulling the waxed twine through the canvas in loops as even as the waves slapping against the hull, ______ her more than his words did, and by the time the island came into view, she could close a seam on her own.
input.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: were teaching
taught
teaching
have taught
input.explanation: 이 문장의 주어는 단수 명사 "The rhythm"이고, 콤마 사이의 긴 분사구(pulling ... hull)는 삽입된 수식어일 뿐이다. 따라서 단수 주어와 맞으면서 지문의 과거 시제(spoke, did, came, could)와도 맞는 정동사가 필요하므로 B "taught"가 정답이다. A는 과거 시제는 맞지만 복수형이어서, 가까이 있는 "hands"나 "waves"에 잘못 맞춘 것이다. C는 분사라서 문장에 정동사가 없게 된다. D는 복수형인 데다 현재완료여서 서술 시제와도 맞지 않는다.
input.explanation_en: The subject of this sentence is the singular noun "The rhythm." The long phrase between the commas (pulling ... hull) only modifies it. So you need a main verb that is singular and also matches the passage's past tense (spoke, did, came, could). That makes B, "taught," the answer. A is in the past tense, but it's plural, so it wrongly agrees with nearby nouns like "hands" or "waves." C is a participle, which leaves the sentence without a main verb. D is plural and in the present perfect, so it doesn't match the narration's tense either.
input.design: 긴 삽입 분사구 안에 복수 명사(hands, waves)를 넣어 주어와 동사의 수 일치를 흐리게 했다. 동시에 시제(과거)와 정동사 여부까지 확인해야 하는 두 단계 판단이 필요하도록 설계했다.

content.text:
Design: a literary excerpt with a long appositive/modifier before a main-clause boundary.

Passage: "Rolf had boarded with the Hubers for three winters, sleeping on a cot wedged between their wardrobe and the stove. The key to his parents' apartment on Wiedner Hauptstraße, a brass thing he carried in his coat pocket like a coin he could not bring himself to ______ the rooms there stood empty, their windows still taped from the war."

Wait: "a brass thing he carried... like a coin he could not bring himself to spend" — sentence subject "The key... spend" needs verb. Better: make a complete independent clause then boundary.

"Rolf turned the brass key over in his palm, the key to his parents' apartment on Wiedner Hauptstraße, which he had not unlocked since ______ the rooms there stood empty, their windows still taped from the war." Blank after "since 1945"? The blank goes after the word "1945"; options: "1945; meanwhile," hmm. Options: A "1945, the", B "1945; the"... but rule says don't repeat the word before blank as first word. So blank right after "1945" with options being punctuation only: A ", " B ";" C "," + "and" ... Let's: A ", and, " hmm. Options: A "1945" can't. Let me do options: A ":" no, colon also works. Use: A ", " (comma splice), B "; meanwhile," , C ", meanwhile," , D "; meanwhile". "Meanwhile" fits contextually loosely. Fine; B correct.

input.passage: Rolf turned the brass key over in his palm. It belonged to his parents' apartment on Wiedner Hauptstraße, a place of high ceilings and a piano no one had played since 1945______ he slept on a narrow cot in the Hubers' kitchen, wedged between the stove and a wardrobe that smelled of camphor.
input.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: , meanwhile,
; meanwhile,
, meanwhile
; meanwhile
input.explanation: 빈칸 앞 "It belonged ... since 1945"는 긴 동격구로 끝나는 독립절이고, 빈칸 뒤 "he slept ..."도 독립절이다. 두 독립절을 접속부사 meanwhile로 이으려면 앞에 세미콜론, 뒤에 쉼표를 써야 하므로 B가 정답이다. A와 C는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어 comma splice가 된다(meanwhile은 등위접속사가 아니다). D는 세미콜론은 맞지만 문장 앞머리 접속부사 meanwhile 뒤에 쉼표가 빠져 있다.
input.explanation_en: The part before the blank, "It belonged ... since 1945," is an independent clause, even though it ends with a long appositive. The part after the blank, "he slept ...," is also an independent clause. If you join two independent clauses with the conjunctive adverb "meanwhile," you need a semicolon before it and a comma after it, so B is correct. A and C use only a comma to join the two clauses, which makes a comma splice, because "meanwhile" is not a coordinating conjunction. D has the correct semicolon, but it leaves out the comma that should follow "meanwhile" at the start of the clause.
input.design: 긴 동격 수식어 때문에 앞 절의 경계가 흐려지게 했고, 세미콜론과 쉼표의 조합을 비교해야만 답이 나오도록 선택지를 구성했다.

input.passage: Triboluminescence, the flash of light some crystals emit when they are crushed or scratched, has been observed for centuries, yet it has long resisted careful study because each flash lasts only microseconds and occurs unpredictably as a crystal fractures. Many researchers assumed that the light arises mainly from electrical discharges: when a crystal splits, opposite charges accumulate on the newly separated faces, and the surrounding air glows as those charges neutralize. In 2021, a team led by materials chemist Lena Okafor tested this assumption by fracturing sucrose and europium-doped crystals inside a vacuum chamber, where no air was available to produce such a glow. Using a high-speed spectrometer synchronized with a mechanical press, the team recorded emission spectra at the instant of fracture. Although the sucrose samples became nearly dark in the vacuum, the europium-doped crystals continued to emit light with spectral peaks matching the europium ions themselves, suggesting that in some materials mechanical stress directly excites atoms within the crystal rather than merely triggering a discharge in the surrounding gas.
input.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: An experiment that removed air from around fracturing crystals indicated that the light from certain crystals can originate inside the material rather than from discharges in the surrounding gas.
An experiment that removed air from around fracturing crystals indicated that triboluminescence in all crystals is produced by electrical discharges between newly separated faces.
An experiment that removed air from around fracturing crystals indicated that sucrose emits more intense light than europium-doped crystals when stress is applied.
An experiment that removed air from around fracturing crystals indicated that high-speed spectrometers are the main reason triboluminescence was difficult to study for centuries.
input.explanation: 진공 실험에서 수크로스는 거의 빛나지 않았지만 유로퓸 결정은 유로퓸 이온 고유의 스펙트럼으로 계속 빛났고, 이는 일부 물질에서는 응력이 결정 내부 원자를 직접 들뜨게 함을 시사한다. 따라서 A가 정답이다. B는 수크로스 결과만 일반화한 것으로, 유로퓸 결과와 '모든 결정'이라는 표현에 어긋난다. C는 진공에서 수크로스가 거의 어두워졌다는 내용과 반대이다. D는 연구를 어렵게 한 원인을 잘못 짚었다. 연구가 어려웠던 이유는 빛이 짧고 예측할 수 없었기 때문이고, 분광기는 연구에 쓰인 도구일 뿐이다.
input.explanation_en: In the vacuum, the sucrose went nearly dark, but the europium-doped crystals kept glowing with spectral peaks that match europium ions. That suggests stress can excite atoms inside some crystals directly, so A is correct. B takes the sucrose result and stretches it to "all crystals," which the europium result contradicts. C reverses the text, since the sucrose became nearly dark. D gets the cause of the difficulty wrong: the flashes were hard to study because they were brief and unpredictable, and the spectrometer was simply the tool used in the experiment.
input.design: A, B, D는 모두 지문의 일부 내용(진공 실험, 기존의 방전 가설, 분광기, 연구가 오래 어려웠다는 점)을 근거로 삼는다. 두 결정의 결과를 서로 비교해야 오답을 배제할 수 있다. 네 선택지는 모두 같은 문장 틀로 썼다.

input.passage: In 1921, Stanford psychologist Lewis Terman began following roughly 1,500 California schoolchildren who had scored exceptionally high on IQ tests. Terman expected that the group, later nicknamed the "Termites," would prove that measured intelligence reliably predicts success in adulthood, and many participants did go on to earn advanced degrees and respectable incomes. Yet when researchers continued tracking the participants for decades after Terman's death in 1956, a more complicated picture emerged. Among the men, those who had achieved the most professionally were not distinguished from the least successful by their childhood IQ scores, which were similarly high across the group. Instead, the most accomplished men had been rated, both by themselves and by their parents, as more persistent and more confident in their goals. Moreover, despite their gifts, none of the participants won a Nobel Prize, whereas two children Terman had tested and excluded for insufficient scores later did.
input.question: According to the text, what did researchers find when they compared the most and least professionally successful men in Terman's study?
options: The most successful men had scored noticeably higher on childhood IQ tests than the least successful men had.
The most successful men had more often earned advanced degrees, which explained their greater income later in life.
The most successful men differed from the least successful mainly in traits such as perseverance and self-assurance rather than in tested intelligence.
The most successful men had been more often excluded from Nobel consideration than the least successful men had.
input.explanation: 지문은 가장 성공한 남성과 가장 덜 성공한 남성이 어린 시절 IQ로는 구별되지 않았고, 대신 끈기와 목표에 대한 자신감에서 차이가 났다고 말하므로 C가 정답이다. A는 Terman의 원래 예상과 같은 방향이지만, 지문은 IQ 점수가 집단 전체에서 비슷하게 높았다고 명시하므로 틀렸다. B는 많은 참가자가 고급 학위를 받았다는 내용을 가져왔지만, 지문은 학위를 두 집단 간 차이의 원인으로 제시하지 않는다. D는 노벨상 관련 내용을 왜곡했다. 지문에서 노벨상은 참가자 전체와 제외된 아이들을 비교할 때만 나오며, 남성 참가자 두 집단을 비교하는 맥락이 아니다.
input.explanation_en: C is correct. The text says the most and least accomplished men were not distinguished by childhood IQ, which was similarly high across the group, but by being more persistent and more confident in their goals. A matches what Terman expected, but it contradicts the finding that the IQ scores were similar. B takes the detail that many participants earned advanced degrees, but the text never presents degrees as what separated the two groups. D distorts the Nobel detail: that comparison is between participants and the children Terman excluded, not between more and less successful men.
input.design: 질문에 있는 '비교'를 정답에 나오는 IQ 외 특성 결과와 연결해야 하는 두 단계 세부 정보 문항이다. A·B·D는 모두 지문의 실제 정보(IQ에 대한 예상, 학위, 노벨상)를 사용해 정답처럼 보이게 했다.

input.passage: Rain drummed on the tin roof of the shelter as Mara sorted through the donation box, pushing aside a cracked headlamp and a bag of stale trail mix. Then her fingers closed around something small and cold. The thin gold band, engraved on its inner surface with two sets of initials and a date from the summer of 1958, ______ exactly like the one her grandmother had worn until the day she died. Mara held it up to the gray light for a long moment before reaching for the shelter logbook and a pencil.
input.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: look
were looking
looked
having looked
input.explanation: 이 문장의 주어는 단수 명사 'band'이고, 'engraved ... 1958'은 주어와 동사 사이에 끼어든 수식어구이므로 빈칸에는 단수 주어와 일치하는 정동사가 필요하다. 또한 지문 전체가 과거 시제(drummed, closed, held)로 서술되므로 C(looked)가 수 일치와 시제를 모두 만족한다. A는 현재형 복수 동사로, 단수 주어와도 맞지 않고 과거 시제 서술과도 어긋난다. B는 과거 시제이지만 바로 앞의 복수 명사 'initials'에 끌린 복수 동사여서 단수 주어 'band'와 일치하지 않는다. D는 분사이므로 문장에 정동사가 없게 되어 완전한 문장이 되지 않는다.
input.explanation_en: The subject of this sentence is the singular noun "band," and the phrase "engraved ... 1958" is a modifier that comes between the subject and the verb, so the blank needs a finite verb that agrees with a singular subject. The whole passage is also told in the past tense (drummed, closed, held), so C ("looked") fits both the agreement and the tense. A is a plural present-tense verb, so it doesn't agree with the singular subject and it breaks the past-tense narration. B is past tense, but it's plural because it's been pulled toward the nearby plural noun "initials," so it doesn't agree with "band." D is a participle, which leaves the sentence without a main verb, so the sentence is incomplete.
input.design: A long modifier with a plural noun ("initials") sits between the singular subject and the blank, which sets a trap for students who skim. To get the answer, students have to check subject-verb agreement and also confirm the past-tense narration. Each wrong choice is partly right: B has the correct tense, A matches the nearby plural noun, and D sounds descriptive.

input.passage: Every winter since his wife's death, Gunnar had kept the harbormaster's house in Húsavík as quiet as the frozen slips below it. But the routine he had built over eleven dark seasons—coffee at five, a solitary walk along the breakwater, tide ledgers until noon—______ apart within a week of the gray dog's arrival, when his daughter and grandsons began stopping by each afternoon to feed the animal, which had taken to sleeping on his porch.
input.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: were coming
have come
come
came
input.explanation: 이 문장의 주어는 단수 명사 'the routine'이고, 그 뒤의 관계절과 대시 사이에 들어간 목록(coffee, walk, ledgers)은 삽입된 수식어일 뿐이다. 또 이야기 전체가 과거 시제(had kept, began)로 서술되므로 단수 주어와 맞으면서 과거 시점을 나타내는 D 'came'이 정답이다. A 'were coming'은 과거 시제지만 복수 동사라서 단수 주어와 맞지 않는다. B 'have come'은 복수형이고 현재완료라서 과거 서술과도 어긋난다. C 'come'은 복수 현재형이므로 수 일치와 시제 둘 다 틀렸다.
input.explanation_en: The subject of this sentence is the singular noun "the routine." The relative clause and the list set off by dashes (coffee, walk, ledgers) are just modifiers that come between the subject and the verb. The story is also told in the past tense ("had kept," "began"), so you need a verb that is singular and past: D, "came." A, "were coming," is past tense, but it's a plural verb, so it doesn't agree with "routine." B, "have come," is plural, and it's in the present perfect, which clashes with the past-tense narration. C, "come," is a plural present-tense form, so it gets both agreement and tense wrong.
input.design: A long relative clause and a dash-enclosed plural list separate the singular subject from the verb, which tempts plural forms. Students also have to check tense against the past-tense narration, which means making two decisions.

content.text:
Need a passage: literary fiction, Anaya and Rajesh rooftop laundry contest. Transition with logic-derived relation. Correct at B.

Design: concession then reversal? e.g., "Anaya had sworn she would not escalate after Rajesh installed a tarp canopy over his line. ______, by Thursday she had dragged her mother's ceiling fan up three flights and wired it to an extension cord." Correct: "Nevertheless," Distractors: "Consequently," (partially — his tarp causing her escalation, but her vow makes contrast), "Similarly," (both escalate), "For example,". Hmm "Consequently" partially plausible. Good medium.

input.passage: By the third week of the monsoon, the rooftop of the Shanti Niwas building had become a battlefield of clotheslines. When Rajesh stretched a blue tarp above his shirts and declared it "a scientific advantage," Anaya told her sister that she refused to sink to his level; the contest, she insisted, would be won by patience and good wringing alone. ______ by Thursday she had hauled her mother's pedestal fan up four flights of stairs, run an extension cord through the stairwell window, and aimed the whirring blades squarely at her damp dupattas.
input.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
options: Consequently,
Nevertheless,
Similarly,
For example,
input.explanation: 앞 문장에서 Anaya는 Rajesh처럼 장비를 쓰지 않고 인내와 손빨래 짜기만으로 이기겠다고 다짐한다. 그런데 다음 문장에서 그녀는 선풍기를 옥상까지 끌고 올라가 정반대 행동을 하므로, 다짐과 실제 행동이 어긋나는 대조를 나타내는 B가 맞다. A는 Rajesh의 방수포가 그녀의 대응을 불렀다고 볼 수 있어 그럴듯하지만, 바로 앞 문장의 핵심은 '그와 같은 수준으로 내려가지 않겠다'는 다짐이고, 이 다짐에서 선풍기 사용이 결과로 나올 수는 없다. C는 두 사람 모두 장비를 동원했다는 점에서 유사해 보이지만, 이 문장의 초점은 Anaya 자신의 말과 행동이 어긋난다는 데 있다. D는 선풍기 사용을 인내 전략의 한 예로 만들어 버리므로 논리에 맞지 않는다.
input.explanation_en: In the previous sentence, Anaya vows to win with patience and wringing alone instead of copying Rajesh's gadgets. Then the next sentence shows her doing the opposite by dragging a fan up to the roof, so B is correct because it signals a contrast between her vow and what she actually does. A may seem reasonable, since Rajesh's tarp could have provoked her. But the key point of the sentence right before the blank is her promise not to sink to his level, and using a fan can't be a result of that promise. C picks up on the fact that both neighbors end up using equipment, but this sentence is about Anaya's own words clashing with her actions. D doesn't work because it would make the fan an example of her patience-only strategy.
input.design: 빈칸 앞에 어휘 단서 없이 다짐을 두고 뒤에 그 다짐을 깨는 행동을 놓아, 양보 후 반전 관계를 찾게 했다. A(원인 방향)와 C(두 사람의 유사성)는 일부 근거가 있어서 지문과 비교해야만 배제할 수 있다.

input.passage: In February 1840, representatives of the British Crown and more than five hundred Māori rangatira (chiefs) signed the Treaty of Waitangi, a document intended to establish British authority in New Zealand. The treaty existed in two versions, English and Māori, and most chiefs signed the Māori text. In the English version, chiefs ceded "sovereignty" to Queen Victoria.
