The Māori version, however, used the word kawanatanga, a newly coined term derived from "governor," while guaranteeing the chiefs tino rangatiratanga, or full chiefly authority, over their lands and villages. __Many historians argue that a chief reading the Māori text would reasonably have understood himself to be granting the Crown a limited power to govern settlers, not surrendering control over his own people and territory.__ This gap helps explain why disputes over land ownership erupted within a few decades and why the treaty remains central to legal claims in New Zealand today.
input.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It offers evidence that the British negotiators deliberately mistranslated the treaty to deceive the chiefs who signed it.
It explains why most Māori chiefs chose to sign the Māori version of the treaty rather than the English version.
It presents a historians' claim that the later land disputes discussed in the text were caused mainly by settlers ignoring both versions of the treaty.
It spells out what the wording differences described earlier likely meant to signatories, setting up the text's account of later conflict.
input.design: 오답 A·B·C 모두 지문 요소(번역 차이, 마오리어판 서명, 이후 분쟁)를 일부 활용하지만 밑줄 문장의 실제 역할(앞의 용어 차이 해석→뒤 분쟁 설명의 연결)과 어긋나게 설계해, 앞뒤 문장을 이어 읽어야 정답을 고를 수 있게 했다.
input.explanation: 밑줄 문장은 앞에서 소개한 kawanatanga와 tino rangatiratanga라는 용어 차이를 받아, 서명한 추장들이 이를 실제로 어떻게 이해했을지 해석해 주고, 이어지는 토지 분쟁 설명의 근거가 되므로 D가 정답이다. A는 번역 차이를 다루지만, 고의로 속였다는 의도는 지문에 언급되지 않는다. B는 추장들이 마오리어판에 서명한 사실을 활용하지만, 밑줄 문장은 그 선택의 이유를 설명하지 않는다. C는 이후 분쟁과 연결되지만, 원인을 이주민이 두 판본을 모두 무시한 데서 찾는 것은 지문의 '해석 차이'라는 설명과 맞지 않는다.
input.explanation_en: The underlined sentence picks up the wording difference described just before it (kawanatanga versus tino rangatiratanga) and explains how a chief would likely have understood it. That reading then sets up the next sentence about later land disputes, so D is correct. A also deals with the translation, but the text never says the British meant to deceive anyone. B uses the fact that most chiefs signed the Māori text, but the underlined sentence doesn't explain why they made that choice. C ties into the later disputes, but it blames settlers for ignoring both versions, while the text points to a gap in interpretation.

input.passage: Metaphysical poets often borrowed the memento mori, a reminder of death, from devotional writing and turned it to secular ends. In "To His Coy Mistress," Andrew Marvell's speaker builds a three-part argument, conceding first that, with endless time, he would praise his beloved slowly for centuries. The poem's second section, which opens with the famous image of "Time's wingèd chariot hurrying ______ that leisure is impossible: the grave, the speaker warns, offers no embraces. Only in the final section does he urge immediate pleasure as the logical conclusion.
input.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: near," and insists
near"; insists
near," insists
near"—and it insists
input.explanation: 주어 "The poem's second section" 뒤에 쉼표로 시작한 비필수 관계절(which opens ... near)이 끼어 있으므로, 관계절을 닫는 쉼표 뒤에 바로 본동사 insists가 와야 한다. 그래서 C가 정답이다. A는 and 때문에 insists가 관계절 안의 두 번째 동사(opens and insists)가 되어 주절에 본동사가 남지 않는다. B는 세미콜론 앞부분이 동사 없는 불완전한 절이 되고, 닫는 쉼표도 빠져 있다. D는 대명사 it이 주어를 한 번 더 써서 원래 주어가 동사를 잃고, 대시로 연 삽입도 쉼표와 짝이 맞지 않는다.
input.explanation_en: The subject "The poem's second section" is interrupted by a nonessential relative clause that begins with a comma ("which opens ... near"). That clause has to close with a comma, and then the main verb, "insists," comes right after it. That's why C is correct. A adds "and," which makes "insists" a second verb inside the relative clause ("opens and insists"), so the sentence ends up with no main verb. B puts a semicolon after a subject that has no verb, so the part before the semicolon isn't a complete clause, and the closing comma is missing too. D adds the pronoun "it," which repeats the subject and leaves the original subject without a verb; it also mixes a dash with the opening comma, so the interruption isn't punctuated consistently.
input.design: 긴 비필수 관계절과 인용부호가 주어와 본동사 사이에 끼어 있어, 수식절을 닫고 본동사로 연결하는지 판단해야 한다. 오답은 등위접속사, 세미콜론, 대시+대명사를 써서 그럴듯해 보이게 만들었다.

input.passage: Sophia stood at the ferry kiosk on the island of Naxos, holding a ticket she had not yet decided to use. Thirty years earlier, she had promised an old sailor named Stavros that she would come back every summer to wait for his boat at this very dock. She had kept that promise for exactly one summer. ______ she had moved to Athens, married, and let the island fade into a story she rarely told.
input.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
options: After that,
For example,
In contrast,
Similarly,
input.explanation: 빈칸 앞 문장은 소피아가 약속을 단 한 번의 여름 동안만 지켰다고 말하고, 뒤 문장은 그 이후 그녀가 아테네로 이사하고 결혼한 일을 말하므로 시간 순서를 잇는 A가 정답이다. B는 예시를 나타내지만, 이사와 결혼은 한 번 약속을 지킨 일의 예가 아니다. C는 대조를 나타내는데, 뒤 문장은 앞 문장과 맞서는 내용이 아니라 그다음에 일어난 일이다. D는 비슷한 내용을 나타내지만 두 문장은 비슷한 행동을 말하고 있지 않다.
input.explanation_en: The sentence before the blank says Sophia kept her promise for only one summer. The sentence after it tells what happened next: she moved to Athens and got married. Since these events come one after another in time, A is correct. B signals an example, but moving and marrying aren't examples of keeping the promise once. C signals a contrast, but the second sentence doesn't oppose the first; it simply continues the story in time. D signals similarity, but the two sentences don't describe similar actions.
input.design: 빈칸 앞뒤의 'for exactly one summer'와 이후 사건(이사·결혼)으로 시간 순서라는 단서를 분명히 드러내고, 오답은 학생들이 자주 헷갈리는 예시·대조·유사 전환어로 구성했다.

input.passage: Lupita spotted her first, a woman in a gray rebozo waiting beneath the depot's flickering sign. It had been eleven years since the two of them had shared a desk in Señora Ibarra's classroom in Real del Monte. Rosa, still clutching the ticket she had bought for the afternoon bus to Pachuca, smiled politely and asked about Lupita's mother. Lupita answered at length, describing the bakery, the new oven, the nephews who now ran the ______ the whole time, she noticed, Rosa kept glancing past her toward the road.
input.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: counter, and,
counter,
counter;
counter
input.design: Lupita로 시작하는 독립절이 긴 분사구와 목록 뒤에서 끝나고, 'the whole time' 같은 부사구로 시작하는 두 번째 독립절이 이어진다. 그래서 학생은 절 경계를 찾아낸 뒤 알맞은 연결 방식을 골라야 한다. 오답 A는 접속사를 갖췄지만 쉼표 위치가 틀렸고, B는 목록이 이어지는 것처럼 보이게 해 함정이 된다.
input.explanation: 빈칸 앞 'Lupita answered ... ran the counter'는 독립절이고, 뒤의 'the whole time, she noticed, Rosa kept glancing...'도 주어 Rosa와 동사 kept를 갖춘 독립절이다. 두 독립절은 세미콜론으로 연결할 수 있으므로 C가 정답이다. B는 쉼표만으로 두 절을 이어 콤마 스플라이스가 되며, 앞의 목록이 계속되는 것처럼 보여 혼동을 준다. D는 아무 문장부호 없이 두 절을 붙인 무종지문이다. A는 등위접속사 and를 넣었지만 and 뒤에 쉼표를 찍어 접속사와 그 절을 불필요하게 끊어 놓았다.
input.explanation_en: Before the blank, "Lupita answered ... ran the counter" is an independent clause. After it, "the whole time, she noticed, Rosa kept glancing..." is also an independent clause, with its own subject, "Rosa," and its own verb, "kept." A semicolon can correctly join two independent clauses, so C is the answer. B uses only a comma, which creates a comma splice, and it can trick you into thinking the list is still going. D joins the two clauses with no punctuation at all, which makes a run-on sentence. A does include the conjunction "and," but the comma after "and" wrongly separates the conjunction from the clause it introduces.

content.text:
Passage: fiction excerpt. Blank between two independent clauses.

"For twenty years, Amaan and Karim had worked side by side in the tannery beside the river. Lately, they spoke only about leather______ neither man could say when the silence had begun."

Options: A ", neither" no—can't repeat? Rule: don't repeat word before blank as first word. Before blank is "leather"; fine. Options: A) "," (comma splice) B) no punctuation C) "; " D) ", and" ... wait D would also be correct. Use C "." Options: A "," B "" (fused)... options must be strings; use "leather" not allowed. Make options: A ", neither", B " neither", C ". Neither", D ", but neither, man"? Better: blank includes "neither": passage "...about leather______ man could say..." Options: A ", neither" B " neither" C "; neither" D ", neither, and". Hmm D odd. Use D ": and neither"? colon+and is wrong-ish. Better D " and, neither" — weird. Use D ", so neither" — that's actually acceptable-ish semantically wrong but grammatical. Avoid. D "neither," ... I'll use D " but neither" without comma — technically acceptable in short? Not strictly. Choose D ", which neither" — creates "which neither man could say when" ungrammatical. Fine.

input.passage: For twenty years, Amaan and Karim had worked side by side at the tannery on the riverbank, dipping hides into the dye pits each morning. Lately, the two partners spoke only about leather______ man could say exactly when the silence between them had begun.
input.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: , neither
neither
; neither
, which neither
input.explanation: 빈칸 앞 'the two partners spoke only about leather'와 뒤 'neither man could say ...'는 각각 독립절이다. 접속사 없이 두 독립절을 잇는 데는 세미콜론이 맞으므로 C가 정답이다. A는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어 쉼표 스플라이스가 된다. B는 문장부호 없이 이어 붙인 융합문(run-on)이다. D는 'which'로 관계절을 만들지만 뒤 내용이 관계절 구조에 맞지 않아 비문이 된다.
input.explanation_en: The text before the blank ("the two partners spoke only about leather") and the text after it ("neither man could say...") are both independent clauses. When you join two independent clauses without a conjunction, a semicolon works, so C is correct. A uses only a comma, which makes a comma splice. B has no punctuation at all, which makes a run-on sentence. D adds "which" to start a relative clause, but the words after it don't fit that structure, so the sentence becomes ungrammatical.
input.design: 독립절 두 개가 한눈에 보이는 단순한 절 경계 문항으로, 쉼표 스플라이스·융합문·잘못된 관계절을 전형적 오답으로 배치했다.

input.passage: When a suspension of identical silica microspheres is left to settle slowly, the particles can arrange themselves into a highly ordered lattice without any external guidance. Materials scientist Hyun-Woo Baek notes that this process is remarkably ______: even a small fraction of spheres that differ in size disrupts the packing, introducing defects that scatter light randomly and prevent the lattice from reflecting the single, vivid color associated with a photonic bandgap.
input.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
options: spontaneous
sensitive
efficient
reversible
input.explanation: 콜론 뒤 내용은 크기가 다른 입자가 조금만 섞여도 배열이 무너진다는 점, 즉 공정이 작은 변화에 쉽게 영향을 받는다는 것을 설명하므로 B(sensitive)가 정답이다. A(spontaneous)는 첫 문장의 '외부 유도 없이'와 맞아 보이지만 콜론 뒤의 결함 설명을 뒷받침하지 못한다. C(efficient)는 질서 있는 격자 형성과 연결될 듯하나 지문은 효율이 아닌 취약성을 강조한다. D(reversible)는 침강·배열 과정과 그럴듯하게 어울리지만 되돌릴 수 있다는 내용은 지문에 없다.
input.explanation_en: The text after the colon explains that even a few spheres of a different size disrupt the packing, so the process is easily affected by small variations, which makes B ("sensitive") correct. A ("spontaneous") seems to fit the first sentence's "without any external guidance," but it doesn't set up the explanation about defects that follows the colon. C ("efficient") might seem to go with forming an ordered lattice, but the text stresses how fragile the process is, not how efficient it is. D ("reversible") sounds plausible for a settling process, but nothing in the text says the arrangement can be undone.
input.design: If you skim only the first sentence, A looks right, because self-assembly sounds spontaneous. Two pieces of information have to be connected: the blank must match the explanation after the colon about small impurities causing defects.

content.text:
Design: a long appositive/modifier before a clause boundary.

Passage idea: "In 1955, chemists Malcolm Williams, Robert Landel, and John Ferry proposed what became known as the WLF equation, a relation describing how a polymer's relaxation modulus shifts with temperature ______ by applying it, researchers can predict decades of stress decay from short laboratory tests."

The blank sits between the appositive and an independent clause. Correct: "temperature; by applying it," with a semicolon. Wrong choices: comma splice "temperature, by"; no punctuation; and "temperature, and, by" (that one might actually be acceptable, so avoid it). Let the options be: A "temperature, by" (comma splice), B "temperature by" (fused), C "temperature, which, by" (a relative clause would need "researchers can predict ... using it", but "it" is redundant, so it's wrong), D "temperature; by". Option C is a wrong-but-plausible choice. Good.

input.passage: In 1955, chemists Malcolm Williams, Robert Landel, and John Ferry published what is now called the WLF equation, a formula describing how far a polymer's relaxation-modulus curve slides along the time axis when the material is heated or cooled by a given number of ______ applying it, engineers can stitch together brief laboratory measurements taken at several temperatures into a single master curve predicting decades of stress decay.
input.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: degrees, by
degrees by
degrees, which, by
degrees; by
input.explanation: 빈칸 앞은 "chemists ... published ... the WLF equation"이라는 독립절에 긴 동격어구가 붙은 형태이고, 빈칸 뒤 "by applying it, engineers can stitch..."도 주어와 동사를 갖춘 독립절이다. 두 독립절은 세미콜론으로 연결해야 하므로 D가 정답이다. A는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이은 쉼표 오용(comma splice)이다. B는 문장부호 없이 이어 붙인 비문이며, "by applying"이 앞의 "degrees"를 수식하는 것처럼 잘못 읽힌다. C는 관계사 which를 넣어 종속절처럼 보이게 했지만, 절 안에 이미 "it"이 있어 which가 맡을 문법적 역할이 없으므로 비문이 된다.
input.explanation_en: Before the blank you have an independent clause ("chemists ... published ... the WLF equation") followed by a long appositive. After the blank comes another full independent clause, "by applying it, engineers can stitch...," which has its own subject and verb. Two independent clauses can be joined by a semicolon, so D is correct. A joins them with only a comma, which makes a comma splice. B runs the clauses together with no punctuation and makes "by applying" seem to modify "degrees." C adds "which" to make the second part look like a relative clause, but the clause already contains "it," so "which" has no grammatical role and the sentence breaks down.
input.design: I put a long appositive with nested modifiers in front of the clause boundary so the independent clause after it is easy to overlook. A, which uses a comma, and C, which uses a relative pronoun, each seem reasonable at first, so you have to compare the clause structures to rule them out.

content.text: Design: dangling modifier? Or subject-verb agreement with long modifier. Let's do agreement: "The compass, along with the two brass hinges that held its lid and the note tucked beneath them, ______ on the chart table..." Subject compass singular → "was resting"? Options: "were resting", "have rested", "resting", "rests"? Tense: past narrative, so "was resting" vs "rests" wrong tense. Let's make D = "lay". Options: A "lie" (plural present), B "were lying", C "lying", D "lay". Hmm "lay" past of lie singular/plural same — agreement not tested. Use "was": A "were", B "have been", C "being", D "was". Sentence: "...______ waiting on his chart table when Captain Josiah returned..." Fine.

input.passage: Captain Josiah had expected a bill of lading, not a gift. Yet the ornate wooden compass, together with the two brass hinges that held its carved lid and the folded note from Silas Marrow tucked beneath them, ______ waiting on his chart table when he returned from the pilothouse that evening. Josiah turned the instrument over in his hands, unable to decide whether his old rival meant it as a treasure or as a quiet jab at the sandbar that had grounded him the previous week.
input.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: were
have been
being
was
input.explanation: 이 문장의 주어는 단수 명사 'compass'이다. 'together with ... beneath them'은 삽입된 수식어구일 뿐 주어를 복수로 만들지 않는다. 또한 이야기가 과거 시제('returned')로 서술되므로 단수 과거 동사 D가 알맞다. A는 시제는 맞지만 바로 앞의 복수 명사 'hinges'나 'them'에 잘못 일치시킨 복수형이다. B는 복수형인 데다 현재완료여서 과거 시점인 'when he returned'와 어울리지 않는다. C는 분사라서 문장에 정동사가 없게 된다.
input.explanation_en: The subject of this sentence is the singular noun "compass." The phrase "together with ... beneath them" is just an interrupting modifier, so it doesn't make the subject plural. The narration is also in the past tense ("returned"), which means the sentence needs a singular past-tense verb, D. A is in the right tense, but it's plural, as if it agreed with the nearby words "hinges" or "them." B is plural too, and its present perfect form doesn't fit the past moment set by "when he returned." C is a participle, so it leaves the sentence with no main verb.
input.design: 긴 삽입 수식어구(together with + 복수 명사들) 뒤에서 주어-동사 일치와 서사 시제를 함께 확인하게 하여 두 단계 판단을 요구했다.

input.passage:
Text 1
In Leila Benali's short story "The Dye Pits," the tanner Karim hands his apprentice Youssef a costly saffron-dyed goatskin on the eve of the slow season by the river. Youssef assumes the hide is payment before he is let go, and critic Hamid Amrani argues that the story supports this reading: the narrator lingers on Karim's long silences and on the lean months ahead, so the gift works as a quiet farewell.

Text 2
Youssef's suspicion makes sense given how unsure his position is, but the story's closing pages undercut it. There we learn that Karim received a nearly identical hide from his own master in the year he was first trusted to mix the dyes alone. Seen this way, the gift marks succession, not dismissal. The narrator's focus on Karim's silences reflects Youssef's anxious state of mind rather than anything Karim actually intends.
input.question: Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to Amrani's interpretation in Text 1?
options: By arguing that Amrani correctly reads Karim's silences as a farewell but misjudges the reason Karim decides to let Youssef go
By arguing that Amrani treats the apprentice's worried reading of the gift as if it were the story's own judgment of the gift
By arguing that Amrani overstates how clear the story is, since the ending leaves Karim's intentions deliberately unresolved
By arguing that Amrani gives too much weight to the slow season, which the story presents as having no effect on the tannery
input.explanation: Text 2의 저자는 Youssef의 의심이 이해할 만하다고 인정하지만, 결말에서 그 선물이 해고가 아니라 계승을 뜻한다는 점이 드러난다고 보고, 침묵에 대한 묘사도 Youssef의 불안을 반영할 뿐이라고 본다. 따라서 Amrani가 견습생의 두려움 섞인 관점을 작품 자체의 판단으로 착각했다고 반박할 것이므로 B가 정답이다. A는 '침묵=작별'이라는 해석에 동의한다고 하지만, Text 2는 그 해석 자체를 부정한다. C는 Text 2가 결말로 의미를 분명히 정리한다는 점과 맞지 않는다. D는 Text 2가 불경기를 다루지 않으므로 근거가 없다.
input.explanation_en: The author of Text 2 agrees that Youssef's suspicion is understandable, but points out that the ending shows the gift means succession, not dismissal. That author also says the focus on Karim's silences reflects Youssef's anxiety, not Karim's intent. So the author would say Amrani has taken the apprentice's fearful view and treated it as the story's own judgment, which makes B correct. A is wrong because Text 2 rejects the farewell reading altogether; it doesn't just question Karim's motive. C is wrong because Text 2 says the ending makes the meaning clear rather than leaving it unresolved. D is wrong because Text 2 never discusses the slow season or says it doesn't matter.
input.design: The two-step reasoning has the reader connect the ending's revelation with the claim that the narration shows Youssef's anxiety, then turn that into a critique of Amrani's view. Each distractor takes up one detail from the texts (silence, the ending, the slow season) and twists it in the same sentence frame.

content.text:
Design: Literary passage. Sentence: "Lukas, who had sat in the second row of cornets since he was nine, saw it first ______ the director's hands trembled as he lifted the baton, a faint quiver that the older players pretended not to notice."
Hmm, need clause boundary after long modifier. Options: A) first, the director's... comma splice; B) first: the; C) first, and; wait "saw it first, and the director's hands trembled" — grammatical though meaning shift... avoid. Use options: A ", " (comma splice), B ":" correct, C no punctuation (run-on), D ", that" hmm. Let's make D "; and" — semicolon plus and is nonstandard-ish. Better D "first, so" — grammatical? "saw it first, so the hands trembled" illogical but grammatical. Better pick clearly wrong: D "first" with dash? Dash would also be correct. Use D: comma after "Lukas"? Keep simple: A comma, B colon, C none, D "first, which". "saw it first, which the director's hands trembled" ungrammatical. Good.

input.passage: At the first rehearsal of the autumn season, the Kapellmeister raised his baton exactly as he had for forty years. Lukas, who had sat in the second row of cornets since he was nine and knew every gesture of that baton by heart, saw it first ______ the old man's hands were trembling, a faint quiver at the wrist that the senior players would pretend not to notice until the spring.
input.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: first,
first:
first
first, which
input.explanation: 긴 삽입절(who had sat ... by heart)을 걷어내면 주절은 "Lukas saw it first"이고, 빈칸 뒤 "the old man's hands were trembling"도 독립절이다. 뒤 절이 앞의 "it"이 무엇인지 구체적으로 설명하므로 두 독립절을 잇는 콜론을 쓴 B가 정답이다. A는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어 쉼표 오류(comma splice)가 된다. C는 문장부호 없이 두 독립절을 붙여 run-on 문장이 된다. D는 which 뒤에 이미 완전한 절이 와서 관계절이 성립하지 않는다.
input.explanation_en: Take out the long interrupting clause (who had sat ... by heart) and you're left with the main clause "Lukas saw it first." The words after the blank, "the old man's hands were trembling," also make up an independent clause. That second clause explains what "it" is, so a colon between the two independent clauses works, which makes B correct. A joins two independent clauses with only a comma, so it's a comma splice. C puts the two clauses together with no punctuation at all, so it's a run-on. D doesn't work because "which" is followed by a clause that's already complete, so it can't form a relative clause.
input.design: 삽입절 때문에 주절의 주어-동사가 멀어져 절 경계를 놓치기 쉽게 했고, 쉼표·무부호·관계사 오답이 각각 그럴듯하게 읽히도록 구성했다.

input.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- "The Leather Fold" is a 2019 short story by the Mexican writer Lucía Arredondo.
- In the story, Miguel, a bus driver, leaves his cracked leather ticket holder at a repair stall in a mountain depot in Oaxaca.
- When Miguel picks it up, the repairman shows him the initials "R.V.," newly revealed under the worn lining.
- Years earlier, Miguel's mother had told him that his father, Rafael Vega, drove buses on that route before leaving town in 1978.
- The repairman remembers that a driver left the holder at the depot decades ago and never came back for it.
- Critics note that the story ends before Miguel decides whether to look for his father.
input.question: The student wants to explain how Miguel figures out who first owned the object he had repaired. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: In Lucía Arredondo's 2019 short story "The Leather Fold," Miguel, a bus driver, leaves his cracked ticket holder at a repair stall in a mountain depot in Oaxaca.

In "The Leather Fold," the initials "R.V." under the lining, together with the repairman's memory of a driver who abandoned the holder decades ago, lead Miguel to realize it belonged to his father, Rafael Vega.
In "The Leather Fold," Miguel learns that his father, Rafael Vega, left town in 1978, and the story ends before Miguel decides whether to look for him.
In "The Leather Fold," the repairman remembers that a driver left the holder at the depot and never came back for it, a detail critics connect to the story's unresolved ending.
input.explanation: 목표는 Miguel이 수리한 물건의 원래 주인을 어떻게 알아내는지 설명하는 것이다. 이를 위해서는 드러난 이니셜, 아버지 이름에 관한 어머니의 말, 수리공의 기억을 하나로 연결해야 한다. B가 이 단서들을 결합해 Miguel이 깨닫게 되는 과정을 보여 준다. A는 작품 정보와 수리를 맡긴 상황만 제시하고 발견 과정은 빠져 있다. C는 아버지의 이름과 열린 결말을 언급하지만 이니셜이나 수리공의 기억 같은 단서는 쓰지 않는다. D는 수리공의 기억 하나만 들고 결말로 넘어가 버려 주인이 아버지라는 것이 밝혀지지 않는다.
input.explanation_en: Your goal is to explain how Miguel works out who first owned the object he had repaired. That means you need to connect several clues: the revealed initials, what his mother told him about his father's name, and the repairman's memory. B links these clues and shows how Miguel comes to his realization. A gives only background on the story and the repair, with nothing about the discovery. C mentions his father's name and the open ending but leaves out the clues, such as the initials and the repairman's memory. D uses just the repairman's memory and then jumps to the ending, so it never shows that the owner was Miguel's father.
input.design: 정답이 되려면 이니셜, 아버지 이름, 수리공의 기억이라는 세 메모를 연결해야 한다. 오답은 모두 정확한 메모를 쓰지만 배경 정보나 결말 쪽으로 벗어나도록 만들었다. 질문에서는 '아버지'나 '이니셜' 같은 핵심어를 쓰지 않았다.

input.passage: Samuel had been aboard the Delta Belle for only three weeks, but he had already learned that Captain Marsh judged a cub pilot by his errors more than by his successes. The captain, a gaunt man who had memorized every sandbar and snag between St. Louis and New Orleans, rarely raised his voice______ when Samuel mistook a harmless wind reef for a dangerous bluff reef one gray morning, the old pilot simply took the wheel and said nothing for an hour, a silence Samuel found worse than any shout.
input.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: , which
input.explanation: 긴 동격 삽입구를 걷어내면 "The captain rarely raised his voice"가 독립절이고, 빈칸 뒤 "when Samuel mistook..., the old pilot simply took the wheel..." 역시 주어와 동사를 갖춘 독립절이다. 뒤의 절은 선장이 목소리를 높이지 않는다는 사실의 구체적 예이므로 콜론으로 연결한 D가 정답이다. A는 쉼표 하나로 두 독립절을 이어 쉼표 오용(comma splice)이 된다. B는 문장부호 없이 두 절을 붙여 무종지문(run-on)이 된다. C의 관계대명사 which는 뒤에 이미 완전한 절이 와서 수식할 자리가 없으므로 문법적으로 성립하지 않는다.
input.explanation_en: If you strip away the long appositive, you get "The captain rarely raised his voice," which is an independent clause. The part after the blank, "when Samuel mistook..., the old pilot simply took the wheel...," is also a complete independent clause. That second clause is a specific example of the captain's quietness, so a colon is the right way to connect the two, which makes D correct. A joins two independent clauses with only a comma, so it's a comma splice. B puts no punctuation between the clauses, so it's a run-on. C uses the relative pronoun "which," but a complete clause already follows it, so "which" has nothing to do in the sentence and it falls apart grammatically.
input.design: 빈칸 앞에 긴 동격 삽입구를 두고 빈칸 뒤 절을 when 종속절로 시작하게 해서 뒤쪽이 종속절처럼 보이도록 했다. 이 때문에 쉼표나 which를 고르기 쉽다. 정답을 고르려면 두 독립절을 확인하고, 뒤 절이 앞 절의 예시라는 관계까지 파악해야 한다.

input.passage: Many mammals, from rats to rhesus monkeys, eat the placenta shortly after giving birth, a behavior known as placentophagy. A long-standing explanation holds that the placenta replenishes iron and protein lost during delivery. Yet biologist Mark Kristal and colleagues observed that rats fed placenta did not show meaningfully better nutrient levels than rats fed ordinary meat of equal weight. What the placenta-fed rats did show was a stronger natural pain-relieving response during and after birth, an effect that ordinary meat did not produce. Kristal's team traced this effect to a substance in placental tissue and amniotic fluid that appears to amplify the body's own opioid system. Building on such findings, some researchers now suspect that placentophagy is valuable less as a meal than as a source of chemical signals, possibly including ones that influence oxytocin release and early maternal care, though this link has not yet been firmly established.
input.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Evidence from rats suggests that eating the placenta may benefit mammal mothers mainly through its biochemical effects rather than its nutritional value.
Evidence from rats suggests that eating the placenta benefits mammal mothers mainly by restoring the iron and protein lost during birth.
Evidence from rats suggests that eating the placenta triggers oxytocin release that directly strengthens early maternal care in mammals.
Evidence from rats suggests that eating the placenta offers mammal mothers no measurable advantage over eating ordinary meat.
input.explanation: 이 글은 영양 회복 가설이 쥐 실험 결과로 약해졌고, 진통 효과와 화학 신호가 더 중요한 이점일 수 있다고 말하므로 정답은 A이다. B는 글에서 소개만 하고 반박하는 기존 가설을 그대로 주장한다. C는 글 마지막에 나오지만 아직 확인되지 않았다고 밝힌 옥시토신 연결을 확정된 사실처럼 말한다. D는 영양 면에서는 맞지만, 일반 고기에는 없던 진통 효과를 무시한다.
input.explanation_en: The text says the rat findings weakened the nutrient-recovery hypothesis and points instead to pain relief and chemical signals as the likely benefits, so A is correct. B states the older hypothesis, which the text brings up only so it can challenge it. C treats the oxytocin link as fact, but the text says that link has not yet been firmly established. D holds up only for nutrition, since it ignores the pain-relieving effect that ordinary meat did not produce.
input.design: 네 선택지 모두 같은 문장 틀을 쓴다. 오답에는 글에서 반박된 기존 가설, 아직 추측 단계인 옥시토신 연결, 영양 비교 결과만 일반화한 진술이 하나씩 들어 있다. 그래서 정답을 고르려면 반박된 내용, 실험 결과, 추측의 정도를 서로 연결해서 읽어야 한다.

input.passage: Hassan set the paper parcels on the rim of the dyeing vat and waited for his brother to open them. Inside were powders he had traded for in Fez over three long weeks: a saffron yellow, an indigo deep enough to look black in shade, and a crimson pressed from insects that only one merchant still sold. Youssef turned the crimson packet over in his stained hands without a word. To Hassan, the gift ______ to Youssef, who had dyed hides the same three colors for twenty years, it sounded like a verdict that those colors were no longer good enough.
input.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: was simply a gesture of admiration;
was simply a gesture of admiration,
was simply a gesture of admiration, and
was simply a gesture of admiration
input.design: 빈칸 뒤 절이 'to Youssef, who…years,'라는 긴 삽입 수식어로 시작해 독립절 경계가 가려지도록 했고, 쉼표+and처럼 부분적으로 그럴듯한 오답을 배치했다.
input.explanation: 'To Hassan, the gift was simply a gesture of admiration'과 'to Youssef, … it sounded like a verdict …'는 각각 완전한 독립절이므로, 둘을 잇는 데는 세미콜론이 알맞다. 그래서 정답은 A이다. B는 독립절 두 개를 쉼표 하나로만 이어 쉼표 오용(comma splice)이 된다. C의 쉼표+and는 문법적으로는 가능해 보이지만, 'to Hassan'과 'to Youssef'를 맞세우는 대조 구조에서 and를 쓰면 'admiration, and to Youssef'처럼 이어져 'to Youssef'가 앞 절에 붙는 것처럼 읽힌다. 따라서 두 관점의 대조가 흐려지고 문장도 어색해진다. D는 문장부호가 전혀 없어 두 절이 그대로 붙어 버리는 무종지문(run-on)이 된다.
input.explanation_en: "To Hassan, the gift was simply a gesture of admiration" and "to Youssef, … it sounded like a verdict …" are both complete independent clauses, so a semicolon is the right way to join them. That makes A correct. B links the two independent clauses with only a comma, which creates a comma splice. C's comma plus "and" might look grammatical, but in a sentence built to contrast "To Hassan" with "to Youssef," adding "and" produces "admiration, and to Youssef," which makes "to Youssef" seem attached to the first clause. That blurs the contrast between the two brothers' views and makes the sentence awkward. D uses no punctuation at all, so the two clauses run together into a run-on sentence.

content.text:
Easy 문항: 짧은 수식어가 낀 주어-동사 수 일치. Subject "The watch, with its repaired face," -> singular verb. Correct A: "catches". Others: "catch", "are catching", "have caught". Past tense context? Keep narrative present.

Passage: "Kamau sits near the window of the crowded matatu as it lurches down Ngong Road. On his wrist is his father's watch, the one his father carried home from a war decades ago. A jeweler in town has just restored it. Now the watch, with its newly polished hands, ______ the light each time the vehicle turns, and strangers lean closer to study its mended face."

Subject "watch" singular; modifier "hands" plural distractor. Good.

input.passage: Kamau sits by the window of the crowded matatu as it lurches down Ngong Road toward the city center. On his wrist is his father's watch, the same one his father carried home from a war many years ago. A jeweler in Nairobi has just finished restoring it. Now the watch, with its newly polished hands, ______ the afternoon light each time the vehicle turns, and the strangers beside him lean closer to study its mended face.
input.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: catches
catch
are catching
have caught
input.explanation: 빈칸에 들어갈 동사의 주어는 단수 명사 'the watch'이고, 'with its newly polished hands'는 주어와 동사 사이에 끼어든 수식어일 뿐이다. 따라서 단수 현재형 동사가 필요하며, 지문 전체가 현재 시제(sits, lean)로 서술되므로 A가 정답이다. B, C, D는 모두 복수 주어에 맞는 동사형으로, 수식어 속 복수 명사 'hands'를 주어로 착각하게 만드는 오답이다. 문장의 실제 주어는 단수인 'watch'이므로 B, C, D는 수 일치가 맞지 않는다.
input.explanation_en: The subject of the verb in the blank is the singular noun "the watch." The phrase "with its newly polished hands" is just a modifier that sits between the subject and the verb. That means you need a singular present-tense verb, and the passage is told in the present tense ("sits," "lean"), so A is correct. B, C, and D are all verb forms that go with plural subjects, and they trick you into treating the plural noun "hands" inside the modifier as the subject. Since the real subject, "watch," is singular, B, C, and D don't agree with it in number.
input.design: 주어와 동사 사이에 복수 명사가 든 짧은 수식어 하나를 넣어, 단수 주어와 동사의 수 일치라는 규칙 하나만 묻도록 했다. 오답은 모두 복수형 동사로 구성해 수식어 속 명사를 주어로 착각하는 전형적인 오개념을 노렸다.

input.passage: Before the 1960s, many linguists treated language as a system of grammatical rules that could be described apart from the situations in which people spoke. Anthropologist Dell Hymes argued that this approach missed something essential: knowing a language also means knowing when, where, and with whom particular ways of speaking are appropriate. To study this knowledge, Hymes proposed analyzing "speech events," such as a storytelling session or a council meeting, by attending to features like the setting, the participants, and the norms governing who may speak. __In his work with Chinookan narratives from the Pacific Northwest, for instance, Hymes showed that tellers organized stories into patterned groupings of lines and verses that shifted depending on audience and occasion, structures that earlier transcribers, focused only on vocabulary and grammar, had flattened into ordinary prose.__ For Hymes, such findings demonstrated that the meaning of speech cannot be fully recovered without the context in which it is performed.
input.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It describes a limitation of Hymes's method that later researchers working with Chinookan narratives sought to correct.
It explains why linguists before the 1960s preferred to study grammatical rules rather than features of speech events.
It presents a specific case illustrating the kind of insight that Hymes's approach to studying speech could yield.
It introduces a point of disagreement between Hymes and other anthropologists about how stories should be transcribed.
input.explanation: 밑줄 문장은 "for instance"로 시작하며, 맥락(청중·상황)에 주목하는 Hymes의 분석이 치누크 서사에서 문법 중심 전사가 놓친 구조를 드러냈다는 구체적 사례를 제시하므로 C가 정답이다. A는 Chinookan 서사를 언급하지만 Hymes 방법의 한계가 아니라 성과를 보여 주므로 틀리다. B는 이전 언어학자들이 언급되긴 하나 그들이 문법을 선호한 이유를 설명하지 않는다. D는 전사 방식에 대한 대비가 있긴 하지만 다른 인류학자와의 논쟁이 아니라 Hymes 접근의 유용성을 보여 주는 예시이므로 틀리다.
input.explanation_en: The underlined sentence opens with "for instance" and gives a concrete case: by paying attention to audience and occasion, Hymes found structure in Chinookan narratives that grammar-focused transcribers had missed. That makes C correct. A mentions Chinookan narratives, but the sentence shows something Hymes's method achieved, not a weakness that others had to fix. B is wrong because, although the text mentions earlier linguists, it never explains why they preferred grammar. D picks up on the contrast about transcription, but the sentence isn't describing a debate with other anthropologists. It's an example of how useful Hymes's approach was.
input.design: "for instance"라는 신호와 앞뒤 주장을 연결해야 하며, 오답 A·D는 지문의 치누크·전사 요소를 부분적으로 활용해 정독 비교가 필요하도록 했다.

content.text:
Need literary passage with transition. Design: concession then reversal without lexical cue. E.g., Linh had every reason to concede: Duc had won three rounds, her pho broth was going cold... ______ she stayed crouched over the chalk squares. Answer "Even so," ; distractors "Therefore," "In other words," "Likewise," — need partial plausibility. Maybe use "Accordingly," "Indeed," "Similarly," and "Even so,".

Make it subtler: Duc tossed his pebble wide; he surely knew customers were gathering at his cart. ______ Linh noticed he made no move to leave... Let's write.

input.passage: Before the first motorbikes filled the alley, Linh and Duc had chalked a hopscotch grid between their carts, each betting the whole morning's earnings. By the fourth round, Linh's broth had stopped steaming, and three office workers stood at her empty stool, checking their watches. Any sensible vendor would have called off the game and ladled out the soup. ______ Linh tossed her pebble again, never taking her eyes off Duc's smug grin.
input.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
options: Accordingly,
Indeed,
Similarly,
Even so,
input.explanation: 앞 문장은 손님이 기다리니 분별 있는 상인이라면 게임을 그만뒀을 것이라고 말하고, 뒷 문장은 Linh이 그래도 다시 돌을 던졌다고 말하므로 예상과 반대되는 행동이 나온다. 따라서 양보 후 반전을 나타내는 D가 정답이다. A는 Linh의 행동이 앞 문장의 합리적 판단에서 나온 결과라고 잘못 표현한다. B는 앞 주장을 강조하거나 덧붙이는 말이라서, 그 주장과 어긋나는 행동과 이어지지 않는다. C는 비슷한 행동을 나열할 때 쓰는 말인데, Linh은 '분별 있는 상인'과 반대로 행동한다.
input.explanation_en: The sentence before the blank says that any sensible vendor would stop playing and serve the waiting customers. The next sentence shows Linh doing the opposite: she throws her pebble again. Because what she does goes against what we would expect, the passage needs a transition that shows contrast after a concession, so D is correct. A suggests her choice follows logically from the sensible advice, which it does not. B adds emphasis to the earlier claim, but Linh's action goes against that claim instead of supporting it. C points to a similar action, yet Linh behaves unlike a sensible vendor.
input.design: There is no "but"-type word near the blank. Students have to see that the "sensible vendor" sentence sets up an expectation, and that Linh's action breaks it. If they skim the passage as a steady buildup of tension, A or B can look right.

input.passage: In the 1970s, German choreographer Pina Bausch developed Tanztheater, a form that blends theatrical storytelling with contemporary dance. Her performers often repeated ordinary gestures, such as brushing hair or embracing, until the movements took on new emotional ______ audiences found these repetitions both unsettling and deeply moving.
input.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: weight, and
weight,
weight
weight, and,
input.explanation: 빈칸 앞 "Her performers ... new emotional weight"와 뒤 "audiences found ... moving"은 각각 독립절이다. 두 독립절은 쉼표와 등위접속사로 연결할 수 있으므로 A가 정답이다. B는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이은 쉼표 스플라이스이다. C는 문장부호나 접속사 없이 두 독립절을 붙인 무종지문이다. D는 접속사 and 뒤에 쓸데없는 쉼표가 있어 틀렸다.
input.explanation_en: The text before the blank ("Her performers ... new emotional weight") and the text after it ("audiences found ... moving") are both independent clauses. You can join two independent clauses with a comma plus a coordinating conjunction, so A is correct. B is a comma splice, because a comma alone can't join two independent clauses. C is a run-on sentence, since it puts the two clauses together with no punctuation or conjunction. D adds an extra comma after "and" that doesn't belong there.
input.design: 빈칸 양쪽 독립절이 한눈에 보이게 쓰고, 쉼표+접속사 규칙 하나만으로 풀리게 했다. 오답은 쉼표 스플라이스, 무종지문, 불필요한 쉼표라는 전형적 오개념이다.

content.text:
Design: literary excerpt; skill — finite verb vs participle/infinitive, with long intervening modifier, subject-verb agreement.

Passage idea: "The older woman, who had come to the cove every morning since the funeral and who now sat wrapped in a borrowed rubber suit beside the stranger, ______ the girl's hand and guided it toward the seaweed-slick rock."
Subject "The older woman" singular; need finite past verb "took". Options: A) taking (no main verb), B) took, C) having taken, D) to take. That's all form. Medium needs agreement too? Options: A "were taking" (plural agreement error, finite though), B "took", C "taking", D "having taken". Good: A tempts because "suit"/"funeral"... actually nearby nouns singular. Use "beside the two divers" plural near blank. Fine.

input.passage: At the edge of the cove on Jeju, the haenyeo were already floating beyond the breakers, their orange buoys bobbing like scattered fruit. The older woman, who had come to the rocks every morning since her daughter's funeral and who now sat in silence beside the two young divers drying their masks, ______ the beginner's trembling hand and pressed it flat against the cold, seaweed-slick stone. "Breathe here first," she said. "The sea can wait."
input.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: were taking
took
taking
having taken
input.explanation: 이 문장의 주어는 단수 'The older woman'이고, 그 뒤에 이어지는 두 개의 who 관계절은 수식어일 뿐이므로 빈칸에는 단수 주어에 맞는 정동사가 와야 한다. 또한 빈칸 뒤의 'pressed'와 and로 병렬되므로 과거시제 정동사 B 'took'이 알맞다. A는 정동사이긴 하지만 바로 앞의 복수명사 'divers'에 수를 맞춘 것이라 단수 주어와 일치하지 않는다. C와 D는 분사형이라 문장에 주동사가 없게 되고, 'pressed'와의 병렬도 깨진다.
input.explanation_en: The subject of this sentence is the singular noun "The older woman." The two "who" clauses after it are just modifiers, so the blank needs a finite verb that agrees with a singular subject. The blank is also joined by "and" to the past-tense verb "pressed," so B, "took," is correct. A is a finite verb, but it agrees with the nearby plural noun "divers" instead of the singular subject. C and D are participles, which would leave the sentence without a main verb and break the parallel with "pressed."
input.design: 긴 관계절 두 개가 주어와 동사 사이에 끼어 있고 빈칸 바로 앞에 복수명사 'divers'를 두어 수 일치 함정을 만들었다. 정동사 vs 분사 판단과 'pressed'와의 병렬 확인까지 두 단계 판단이 필요하다.

input.passage: Thermoelectric modules convert heat directly into electricity through the Seebeck effect: when one side of a semiconductor junction is hotter than the other, charge carriers drift toward the cooler side, producing a voltage. Because the devices have no moving parts, engineers have long hoped to attach them to car exhausts and factory chimneys to recover energy that would otherwise be lost. __Yet the very materials that conduct electricity well tend to conduct heat well too, so the temperature difference the module depends on quickly evens out.__ For this reason, most commercial modules convert less than ten percent of the heat passing through them. Researchers at several laboratories are now designing semiconductors laced with nanoscale grain boundaries that scatter heat-carrying vibrations while letting electrons pass, an approach that could loosen this trade-off.
input.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It identifies a physical obstacle that accounts for a limitation described later and motivates the research discussed at the end.
It explains the mechanism by which the Seebeck effect generates a voltage across a semiconductor junction.
It presents evidence that thermoelectric modules are unsuitable for use on car exhausts and factory chimneys.
It describes how nanoscale grain boundaries allow electrons to pass while blocking heat-carrying vibrations.
input.explanation: 밑줄 문장은 전기를 잘 통하는 물질이 열도 잘 통해 온도차가 사라진다는 물리적 장애를 제시하며, 이것이 다음 문장의 낮은 변환 효율(10% 미만)의 원인이 되고 마지막 문장의 나노 구조 연구의 동기가 되므로 A가 정답이다. B는 Seebeck 효과의 작동 원리를 다루는데, 이는 첫 문장의 역할이다. C는 밑줄 문장이 응용을 제약하는 것은 맞지만 부적합하다고 단정하지 않으며, 글은 오히려 해결 노력을 소개한다. D는 마지막 문장의 내용으로, 밑줄 문장은 해결책이 아니라 문제를 제시한다.
input.explanation_en: The underlined sentence names a physical obstacle: materials that conduct electricity well also conduct heat well, which erases the temperature difference. That obstacle explains the low efficiency (under ten percent) mentioned in the next sentence and motivates the nanoscale research described at the end, so A is correct. B describes how the Seebeck effect works, but that is the job of the first sentence. C goes too far: the sentence points to a limitation, but the text never says the modules are unsuitable, and it actually goes on to describe efforts to fix the problem. D restates the final sentence; the underlined sentence presents the problem, not the solution.
input.design: To get this right, students have to connect the underlined sentence to both the efficiency figure after it and the research at the end. B and D describe content from other sentences in the text, and C overstates the limitation the sentence actually describes.

input.passage: Photochromic eyeglass lenses darken outdoors and clear indoors because of molecules embedded in their plastic. In many lenses, these are spirooxazine molecules, which normally hold a folded, colorless shape. When ultraviolet light strikes one, a chemical bond breaks and the molecule unfolds into a flat form that absorbs visible light, tinting the lens. __Yet the flat form is not stable on its own: once ultraviolet exposure stops, heat from the surroundings gradually pushes the molecules back into their folded shape.__ This reversal is why wearers notice that their lenses fade more slowly on a cold day than on a warm one, since lower temperatures supply less of the energy needed to refold the molecules.
input.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It describes the step by which ultraviolet light gives the molecules a form that tints the lens.
It presents an exception showing that some lenses keep their tint after ultraviolet exposure ends.
It explains a process that the text then uses to account for an effect wearers observe.
It introduces a disagreement about whether heat or light controls how the lenses change.
input.explanation: 밑줄 문장은 자외선이 사라진 뒤 주변의 열이 분자를 다시 접힌 형태로 되돌린다는 과정을 설명하고, 다음 문장은 이를 근거로 추운 날 렌즈가 더 천천히 맑아지는 현상을 설명하므로 C가 정답이다. A는 자외선이 분자를 펼치는 단계를 말하는데, 그것은 밑줄 앞 문장의 내용이고 밑줄 문장은 반대 방향의 과정을 다룬다. B는 'Yet'을 예외 제시로 잘못 읽은 것이며, 실제로는 착색이 사라진다는 내용이다. D는 열과 빛이 모두 언급된 점에 기댄 것이지만, 지문에는 어떤 논쟁도 없고 두 요인이 각각 다른 단계를 맡는다고 설명할 뿐이다.
input.explanation_en: The underlined sentence explains how heat refolds the molecules once ultraviolet light is gone, and the next sentence uses that process to explain why lenses fade more slowly on cold days, so C is correct. A describes ultraviolet light unfolding the molecules, but that happens in the sentence before the underlined one, while the underlined sentence covers the reverse process. B misreads "Yet" as signaling an exception, when the sentence actually says the tint goes away. D picks up on the fact that both heat and light are mentioned, but the text describes no disagreement; it just shows each factor driving a different step.
input.design: To answer, students must connect the underlined process to the cold-day effect in the following sentence. A, which matches the sentence before it, and D, which relies on both heat and light being mentioned, are partly supported, so students have to compare them with C to rule them out.

content.text:
Design: a long appositive/modifier before a clause boundary.

Passage: "Priya found the envelope wedged beneath a torn seat on the matatu to Westlands, its stamp faded to the color of weak tea and its postmark dated 1994. The name on the front, a Mrs. Wanjiru Kamau of Ngong Road, belonged to a woman Priya had never heard ______ the return address, scrawled in a careful, slanting hand, gave a street in Kampala."

Wait — the woman now lives three countries away. Let me add that afterward. The blank should follow "of", so the choices shouldn't begin with "of". Options: "of; the", "of, the", "of the", "of, and, the"... Better to focus on the boundary. Choices: A "of, the" (comma splice), B "of; the", C "of the" (run-on), D "of: and the". Medium difficulty needs partially plausible distractors. Alternative set: A "of, the", B "of—the", C "of the", D "of, and, the". Since the "of" is before the blank, each option starts with a punctuation mark, which is fine. I'll go with: A ", the" B "; the" C " the" D ", and, the".

input.passage: Priya found the envelope wedged beneath a torn seat on the matatu to Westlands, its stamp faded to the color of weak tea and its postmark dated 1994. The name on the front, a Mrs. Wanjiru Kamau of Ngong Road, belonged to a woman Priya had never heard of______ the return address, written in a careful, slanting hand, gave a street in Kampala. Later that week, a clerk at the post office told her that Mrs. Kamau had long since moved to Lusaka.
input.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: , the
; the
the
, and, the
input.explanation: 빈칸 앞 "The name on the front, ... belonged to a woman Priya had never heard of"는 삽입된 동격구가 있어도 완전한 독립절이고, 빈칸 뒤 "the return address ... gave a street in Kampala"도 독립절이다. 두 독립절은 세미콜론으로 연결할 수 있으므로 B가 정답이다. A는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어 comma splice가 된다. C는 문장부호 없이 두 절을 붙인 run-on 문장이다. D는 등위접속사 and를 쓴 점은 맞지만 and 뒤에 쉼표를 두어 접속사와 이어지는 절을 불필요하게 갈라놓는다.
input.explanation_en: The part before the blank, "The name on the front, ... belonged to a woman Priya had never heard of," is a complete independent clause even with the appositive in the middle, and the part after it, "the return address ... gave a street in Kampala," is also an independent clause. A semicolon can join two independent clauses, so B is correct. A connects the two clauses with only a comma, which makes a comma splice. C puts no punctuation between the clauses, which creates a run-on sentence. D is right to use the conjunction "and," but the comma after "and" wrongly separates the conjunction from the clause it introduces.
input.design: The commas around the appositive and the clause-final preposition "of" hide where the first clause ends. Students have to find both independent clauses and then compare a comma splice, a run-on, and a conjunction with a misplaced comma.

input.passage: Early copies of the Quran were often written in Kufic, a script known for its angular, horizontal letterforms. By the tenth century, however, many copyists had begun to favor Naskh, a rounded script that was easier to read and faster to ______ it eventually became one of the most widely used scripts for manuscripts across the Islamic world.
input.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: write,
write
write, and,
write, and
input.explanation: 빈칸 앞 'By the tenth century ... faster to write'와 뒤 'it eventually became ...'는 모두 독립절이다. 두 독립절은 쉼표와 등위접속사로 이어야 하므로 'write, and'인 D가 정답이다. A는 쉼표만으로 독립절을 이어 쉼표 스플라이스가 된다. B는 아무 부호 없이 두 절을 붙인 무종지문(run-on)이다. C는 'and' 뒤에 불필요한 쉼표를 넣어 접속사와 뒤 절을 부당하게 끊는다.
input.explanation_en: The text before the blank ("By the tenth century ... faster to write") and the text after it ("it eventually became ...") are both independent clauses. To join two independent clauses, you need a comma followed by a coordinating conjunction, so D, "write, and," is correct. A joins the clauses with only a comma, which creates a comma splice. B puts no punctuation between the clauses, which creates a run-on sentence. C adds an extra comma after "and" that wrongly separates the conjunction from the clause it introduces.
input.design: 독립절 두 개가 한눈에 보이게 하고, 쉼표 스플라이스·무종지문·불필요한 쉼표 같은 흔한 오개념을 오답으로 넣어 규칙 하나만으로 풀리게 했다.

input.passage: Magnetorheological fluids consist of tiny iron particles suspended in oil. With no magnetic field present, the particles drift freely and the fluid pours much like motor oil. When a field is applied, however, the particles snap into chains aligned with the field lines, and within milliseconds the fluid stiffens into a near-solid. Because engineers can strengthen or weaken the field continuously, the fluid's resistance to flow is not simply switched on or off but can be ______ to any level between those extremes, a property that makes it useful in seat suspensions that respond to each bump in the road.
input.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
options: reversed
maximized
concealed
calibrated
input.design: 자기장을 '연속적으로' 조절한다는 정보와 '두 극단 사이의 어떤 수준이든'이라는 정보를 함께 읽어야 정답이 나온다. A와 B는 켜고 끄는 전환이나 고체화에서 부분적 근거를 얻어 훑어 읽으면 고르기 쉽게 설계했다.
input.explanation: 지문은 자기장을 연속적으로 세게 하거나 약하게 할 수 있어서 유체의 저항이 켜짐/꺼짐 둘 중 하나가 아니라 두 극단 사이의 어떤 수준으로든 맞춰질 수 있다고 말합니다. 따라서 원하는 정확한 수준으로 맞춘다는 뜻의 D가 정답입니다. A는 자기장을 끄면 유체가 다시 흐른다는 점에서 그럴듯하지만, '되돌린다'는 말은 중간 수준으로 맞춘다는 뜻을 담지 못합니다. B는 유체가 거의 고체로 굳는다는 내용과 연결되지만, 지문이 강조하는 것은 최대치가 아니라 '어떤 수준이든'이라는 범위입니다. C는 저항이 사라진다는 뜻으로 오해할 수 있지만, 숨긴다는 뜻이라 맥락에 맞지 않습니다.
input.explanation_en: The passage says the field can be strengthened or weakened continuously, so the fluid's resistance isn't just on or off—it can be set to any level between the two extremes. That's why D, meaning adjusted precisely to a chosen level, is correct. A seems reasonable because turning off the field lets the fluid flow again, but "reversed" doesn't express setting the resistance to an in-between level. B connects to the fluid stiffening into a near-solid, but the passage stresses "any level," not just the highest one. C might suggest the resistance disappearing, but "concealed" means hidden, which doesn't fit the context.
